docs.title: On top: a provable answer
docs.text:
examples/fintech_audit — a transactions CSV, a budget CSV and a policy doc, no API key. The model never computes the number; plain Python does, and the answer is linked to its evidence:

variance vs budget: +12.5%   ($45,000 actual vs $40,000 budget, 10% policy threshold → over)
answer sha256 5461290d…  ·  context sha256 24449f6f…

re-running the pipeline hashes identically — or verify a saved run:
  reactifact replay <store> --session <id> --verify 24449f6f…

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
EVENT (created/updated)
                                          │
                                          ▼
CONTEXT ───────► ARTIFACTS ──► STEPS REACT ──effects──► EFFECTS
   ▲                 │                                            │
   │                 │                                            │  compile
   └────── CONTEXT' ◄────────────────┘ PATCH ◄────────────────────┘

You describe what data exists, what artifacts exist, and what agents can do with them. The runtime does the plumbing.

docs.title: The mental model
docs.text: Traditional agent reactifact A program follows a graph / plan Agents react to state changes Messages are strings Typed artifacts (Claim, Evidence, Answer, …) Orchestration is explicit Orchestration falls out of the state A unit of work returns a change A step writes effects (effects) — the runtime compiles them Retries/rollback are manual Context is versioned (git-like commits, diff, checkout/at) "Who produced this?" is lost Provenance links every derived artifact to its inputs

docs.title: Why effects instead of "return a change"?
docs.text:
At the heart of the loop is how a step makes a change. Many frameworks ask a unit of work to return its result, and some orchestrator applies it. reactifact inverts authorship: a step states what should change via effects (create / update / delete / link / upsert); the runtime compiles the effect set into one atomic patch — the whole step lands (or none of it does).

async def run(self, doc: Document, turn: Turn, effects: Effects) -> Answer:
    evidence = effects.create(Evidence(...), id="evidence:q1")
    answer = effects.create(Answer(...), id="answer:q1")
    evidence.link("extracted_from", doc)
    answer.link("supported_by", evidence)
    effects.update(turn, status="answered")
    return answer

Because handles are objects, not ids, one statement can reference the artifact created by another — and because the runtime owns the compilation, you never assemble a Patch by hand. Human-in-the-loop is just another effect (human.ask(...)). See Why reactifact for the full argument, and The step contract for details.

docs.title: Why artifacts instead of messages?
docs.text: Messages are opaque; artifacts are inspectable. An Evidence object knows its text, its source, and its score. Because every artifact carries provenance, the runtime can answer "why did the agent say that?" by walking the links Answer —supported_by→ Claim —derived_from→ Evidence —extracted_from→ Doc.

docs.title: Why versioned context?
docs.text:
Every run is a commit. That gives you:

  • Diff — exactly what changed between two turns.
  • Rollback — undo a bad step and re-run from a clean state.
  • Deterministic replays — the same history reproduces the same result.
  • Inspectability — a full, queryable history of everything that happened.

docs.title: Requires
docs.text:
• Python 3.11–3.14 (.venv is managed by uv; CI runs the full suite on all four).
  • pydantic for artifact models; FastAPI/uvicorn only for the web demos.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Two agents, no graph edge declared between them — the second reacts because the first one's output exists, and the answer carries proof of where it came from:

from pydantic import BaseModel

from reactifact import Budget, Context, Runtime, RuntimeResources, step


class Question(BaseModel):
    text: str


class Evidence(BaseModel):
    text: str


class Answer(BaseModel):
    text: str


DOCS = {
    "refund": "Refunds are available within 14 days of purchase.",
    "pricing": "The Pro plan is $49/month, billed annually.",
}


@step(produces=Evidence, consumes=Question)
async def find_evidence(call):
    question = call.trigger
    hit = next((v for k, v in DOCS.items() if k in question.data.text.lower()), None)
    if hit is not None:
        call.effects.create(Evidence(text=hit))


@step(produces=Answer, consumes=Evidence)
async def answer_from_evidence(call):
    evidence = call.trigger
    call.effects.create(Answer(text=evidence.data.text)).link("supported_by", evidence)


ctx = Context(resources=RuntimeResources())
runtime = Runtime(ctx, steps=[find_evidence, answer_from_evidence], budget=Budget(max_runs=10))

ctx.create(Question(text="what's your refund policy?"))
runtime.run()  # search_agent and answer_agent both react — nobody wired them together

answer = ctx.latest(Answer)
evidence = ctx.related(answer.id, "supported_by")[0]
print(answer.data.text)                     # "Refunds are available within 14 days of purchase."
print("supported_by:", evidence.data.text)  # provenance you can trace, not just a string in a log

That is the whole loop: create an artifact → agents react → a patch is applied → the context version advances. Everything else in this documentation builds on that loop.

Ready for something closer to a real app? Quickstart has three runnable, verified snippets — a tool-calling agent, retrieval over your own docs, a session-persisted chat bot — each pointing at the full example it's trimmed from.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
Understand the idea

  • Why reactifact — the design argument: why effects, why no graph, why determinism, why versioned state.
  • Comparison — reactifact vs LangGraph/CrewAI, feature by feature, and when not to use reactifact.
  • Concepts — Context, Artifact, Patch, Step, StepGroup.

Build with it

  • Quickstart — three runnable snippets: tool-calling agent, retrieval over your docs, session-persisted chat bot.
  • Sources — where agents get information from.
  • Providers — wiring an LLM/embedder/image/speech provider into RuntimeResources.
  • Recipes — ready-made search fan-out, ref materialization, lifecycle state machines.
  • Patterns — reusable shapes (reflection, map-reduce, supervisor, …), each backed by a concrete example.

Operate it

  • Observability — every run traces agent spans, reads/writes, LLM calls; offline dashboard, or ship to Langfuse/Postgres.
  • Durability & resume — a session-backed run survives a process restart; what "at-least-once" means and how to make produces idempotent.
  • Logging — correlated structured logs (configure_logging()); each line carries run_id/session_id/agent.
  • Deadlines & shutdown — hard max_seconds, request_stop()/ashutdown(), active_runs() readiness.
  • Troubleshooting — "my agent didn't run" / "ran twice" / "the run stopped early" — organized by symptom, not by feature.
  • Evaluation — multi-level scoring over the final Context (evidence quality, provenance grounding, calculation correctness, …).
  • Branching & merge — fork state, explore alternatives, three-way merge with explicit conflicts.
  • Replay — reconstruct why the agent answered, deterministically, without re-running agents.
  • Visualization & CLI — Mermaid diagrams of the artifact graph and a run's trace; the reactifact command-line tools.
  • API reference — every top-level symbol, one line each.

See it run

  • Examples — thirteen runnable examples you can run.
  • Port matrix — which classic LangGraph/CrewAI/DSPy pattern maps to which example.
  • Design notes — deeper rationale for the adaptive scheduler and the effects → Patch compilation model.

docs.title: A2A (Agent2Agent)
docs.text:
Agent2Agent is an open protocol for agent-to-agent interop: an Agent Card for discovery, Tasks with a lifecycle, and Messages carrying text/file/data parts, over JSON-RPC + SSE. reactifact.a2a speaks it in both directions — call a remote agent, or serve your own — with no extra dependency (the client uses httpx, the server FastAPI from the existing web extra, imported lazily).

The JSON-RPC binding implemented here is the A2A 0.3 wire shape (camelCase fields, kind-discriminated parts).

docs.title: Call a remote agent
docs.text:
A2AClient is the protocol surface; A2AAgentTool wraps it as a reactifact Tool, so an LLMAgent can delegate to a remote agent like any other tool:

from reactifact.a2a import A2AClient, A2AAgentTool

client = A2AClient("https://agent.example.com/a2a", headers={"x-api-key": "…"})
card = await client.fetch_agent_card()          # AgentCard
task = await client.send("Summarise the incident")
print(task.status.state, task.artifacts[0].parts[0].text)

researcher = A2AAgentTool(client, name="researcher")
# agent = create_step_group("lead", steps=[...researcher...])

A2AClient also exposes stream(message) (an async iterator of task/message events over SSE), get_task(id) and cancel_task(id).

docs.title: Run a remote agent as a node
docs.text:
A2AAgentTool is for an LLM loop. To have the runtime schedule a remote agent alongside local ones — the analogue of LangGraph's A2ARemoteGraph — use remote_agent(...): a first-class node that consumes a local artifact, calls message/send, and produces a local artifact, so provenance, budget, guardrails and eval apply as usual:

from reactifact import Consume, Runtime
from reactifact.a2a import remote_agent

translator = remote_agent(
    "translator",
    "https://agent.example.com/a2a",
    consumes=[Consume(Question)],
    output_type=Answer,          # built as Answer(text=reply)
)
Runtime(ctx, groups=[translator, …]).arun()

A remote task in input-required becomes a local PendingQuestion; a later context.resume(...) continues the same remote task and lands the final artifact. Pass message_of= (input → text) and build_output= (reply, input → artifact) when the types have no text field. The lower-level A2ARemoteStep is the Step behind it.

docs.title: Serve reactifact agents
docs.text:
create_a2a_router(agents, ...) returns a FastAPI router: an Agent Card plus a JSON-RPC endpoint where a Task is one conversation:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from reactifact.a2a import create_a2a_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(create_a2a_router([RouteGroup(), …], name="ops-agent"))

It serves GET /.well-known/agent-card.json (and the legacy /.well-known/agent.json) and POST / with message/send, message/stream, tasks/get, tasks/cancel.

A2A reactifact Agent Card (skills) built from the artifact types each agent's steps produce Task one conversation over a Context message/send seed via create_message(ctx, text), run the agents to a fixpoint, read the reply with reply(ctx, seed_id) message/stream (SSE) the working task, a status update per context.announce() progress event, then the final task input-required the run paused on a PendingQuestion; the next message/send with the same taskId resumes it Artifact the reply text as a Part

create_message and reply are the domain hooks (exactly like reactifact.chat): without them the server seeds a UserMessage and replies with the last artifact that has a text field. Pass your own to use the app's real input/output types:

def create_message(ctx, text):
    return ctx.create(Question(text=text)).id

def reply(ctx, seed_id):
    answer = ctx.latest(Answer)
    return answer.data.text if answer else ""

app.include_router(create_a2a_router(GROUPS, create_message=create_message, reply=reply))

docs.title: Interop
docs.text: The server is verified against the official a2a-sdk client (a dev-extra test, not runtime): the reference client resolves our Agent Card and calls message/send, receiving a completed task with the reply artifact — see tests/test_a2a_interop.py. a2a-sdk is only used by that interop test (the a2a dependency group/extra); the runtime itself keeps httpx + FastAPI and nothing else.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Implemented: Agent Card, message/send, message/stream (SSE), tasks/get, tasks/cancel, the input-required ↔ PendingQuestion mapping, and the JSON-RPC binding 0.3. Out of scope: push-notification config, tasks/resubscribe, authenticated extended card, the gRPC and HTTP+JSON (REST) bindings, and any securitySchemes (put auth in front of the router). Tasks are kept in-process (like reactifact.chat) — persist the Context with a Session yourself for durability.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: Top-level symbols exported by reactifact (see reactifact/__init__.py). The format for each group: name — one-line role. Details live in the doc-strings of the modules — see the auto-generated reference for those rendered directly from source (signatures, types, full docstring text) on the docs site, rather than copied here by hand. Per-area pages: Knowledge, Evaluation, Sources, Providers, Recipes, Tracing.

docs.title: Stability
docs.text:
reactifact is pre-1.0 (0.25.1) but not rc — the surface below is the stable contract, not a moving target. It is machine-checked: tests/test_public_api.py pins reactifact.__all__ and the canonical submodule exports (reactifact.step, reactifact.consume, reactifact.chat, reactifact.tools.use, reactifact.eval, reactifact.recipes, reactifact.providers, reactifact.tracing), so a new export there has to be added deliberately (and documented), never by accident.

  • Public API = every name in reactifact.__all__ and the pinned submodule __all__ above. The optional reactifact.knowledge, reactifact.viz, reactifact.quick, reactifact.redaction and reactifact.audit surfaces are documented and semver-governed, but join the freeze test as part of the 1.0 checklist. If it's importable from reactifact but not in __all__, it's an internal detail with no compatibility guarantee — e.g. reactifact.relations.RelationGraph and reactifact.commit_log.CommitLog exist because Context was split into smaller modules for readability, but neither is exported: Context is the supported surface, they are not.
  • SemVer, pre-1.0 style: a minor bump (0.24.0 → 0.25.0) may add symbols or, rarely, change behavior in a way CHANGELOG.md marks Breaking — pre-1.0 minors are where reactifact is still allowed to correct a design mistake. A patch bump (0.14.0 → 0.14.1) never removes or renames a public symbol and never changes documented behavior, only fixes bugs against it.
  • Deprecation: a symbol on its way out stays importable and keeps working for at least one minor release; it is marked deprecated in the docstring and CHANGELOG.md (with the replacement) before any removal, and removal only happens in a minor release under a ### Breaking heading. If a removal cannot wait, the ### Breaking entry and the migration guide must say so explicitly (0.23's Effects.ask/resume/act is such an exception).
  • Every breaking change is called out in CHANGELOG.md under a ### Breaking heading, even in a pre-1.0 release — see release.md. If you only read one section before upgrading, read that one.
  • 1.0 means this page stops moving: the release checklist is the bar for leaving pre-1.0; after that, SemVer 1.x applies (no breaking change in a minor).
  • Anything under reactifact.cli.* beyond the documented python -m reactifact … subcommands, and anything in a module's tests-only helpers, is implementation detail regardless of whether it happens to be importable.

docs.title: Import map
docs.text:
reactifact top-level is a curated shortcut for the core primitives and the main facades. Specialized objects live in their canonical submodule; import from there when you want the full surface:

What Canonical import steps, groups, return-style instructions, input annotations from reactifact.step import Step, StepGroup, Emit, Scope, Unscoped, Wakes consume declarations and lifecycle variants from reactifact.consume import Consume, OnCreate, IdempotentConsume, JoinConsume chat hooks and memory from reactifact.chat import Chat, ChatAssistant, ChatReply, ChatMemory tool loops from reactifact.tools.use import ToolUse, NativeToolUse, ToolUseHITL an agent/subflow as a tool from reactifact.tools.agent import AgentAsTool providers and provider specs from reactifact.providers import LLMProvider, LLMSpec recipes from reactifact.recipes import Route, ScopedCleanup, TurnContextStep verification from reactifact.verify import Verify

reactifact.__all__ remains the shortcut for Context, Artifact, Step, StepGroup, Consume, Effects, Runtime, Pipeline, Chat, Budget, the lifecycle consumes, CurrentRequest, the input annotations, and tools. The freeze test pins both the top-level set and the canonical submodule __all__ lists.

docs.title: Quick on-ramp (reactifact.quick)
docs.text:
Thin sugar over the primitives below for the four common first tasks — every object exposes the real .agent/.agents and the run's .context, so it graduates to Consume/Step/Effects with nothing to rewrite. See Quickstart §0.

Symbol Role agent(system, schema) one structured LLM call → one typed artifact rag(sources) retrieval → materialize → answer, with supported_by provenance tools_agent(system, tools, human=False) LLM + tools (human=True → HITL asks) chat_agent(groups) a configured Chat (in-memory store by default) Question / Doc / Answer the generic artifact models the facade uses

docs.title: Context & state
docs.text: Symbol Role Context versioned working state; resources; request (the active turn's per-request mapping); queries; latest(Model); announce; diff/checkout (at(version) for a snapshot); compact(keep_commits=, keep_versions=) to bound history (compacted_at); apply_commit(commit) replays a commit into the live state (the append-only session load path) View result of a typed join query (context.view(...)) RuntimeResources providers + sources + app resources; register(Type, instance, owned=False) / get(Type) / require(Type) / has(Type) for typed collaborators (ResourceKey[T] when two of one type); an explicit registration wins over artifact resolution for that type; owned=True hands the resource to aclose(); string get/set stay as the additional escape hatch; redactor= scrubs trace text; trace_truncate= caps artifact/response JSON kept in a trace (None = no clip) — deprecated fallback (emits DeprecationWarning), prefer TraceLimits(max_data_chars=…); await resources.aclose() closes owned resources (LIFO) and then the llm/embedder HTTP clients (duck-typed, async aclose() or sync close()) — call it yourself at real shutdown; record_tool_args=True puts tool args on ToolRun (scrubbed by redactor=) ResourceKey[T] a typed handle for registering two resources of one type (primary/replica, per-tenant) ResourceScope / RuntimeResources.scope(factory) async with builder that creates resources on the current loop and closes them on exit — the loop-safe way to own providers (see the class docstring) current_request() the active turn's request mapping (same as StepCall.request) CurrentRequest read-only Mapping of Runtime.arun(request=...); inject request: CurrentRequest (or use Step.request/call.request) instead of a contextvar Commit, Read, Write version bookkeeping and recorded provenance ops ContextCheckpoint lightweight view of one commit (id, version, parent_ids, created_at, author, message, writes); context.checkpoints(), context.checkpoint(id/version), context.at(checkpoint)

docs.title: Artifacts & changes
docs.text: Symbol Role Artifact immutable (id, version, data, content_hash) handle; history lives in Context (artifact_version/version_history/find_versions) ArtifactConflict optimistic-concurrency failure: effects.update(..., expected_version=…) / Context.update expected a different version; the runtime validates the whole generation before applying any patch register_type(Model, *, type_id=, aliases=, migrate=) (reactifact.types) stable persisted type identity: a rename/move of a model no longer breaks loading old sessions/commits/events. type_id_of/resolve/migrate_payload; default id is the qualified name Patch the runtime's compiled change-set (transport); steps write effects (effects/call.effects), Patch is assembled by the runtime reactifact.operations (Create/Update/Delete/Link/Unlink/Relation) the compiled operations a patch carries (§12) Create, Update, Delete, Link, Unlink, Relation op records from which patches are built

docs.title: Groups & steps
docs.text: Symbol Role StepGroup optional thin container: name, steps, concurrency_limit, retry, timeout, fallback; step consumes derive triggers. fallback=Step runs once after retries are exhausted, in a fresh effects slot (failed-attempt effects are discarded) create_step_group constructor-style StepGroup builder — no subclassing needed; accepts retry=/timeout= Runtime(steps=..., groups=...) dispatches steps and groups together (steps first). Each raw Step is wrapped in an implicit group of one. Chat(steps=..., seed_type=..., answer_type=...) typed chat facade: invoke/stream/history/answer, seed_factory, per_turn, resume_pending=, router(), http(), test_client(), traces=/lifespan=, store=. A pending PendingQuestion makes the default reply waiting: true with a structured question; resume_pending=True makes the next turn its answer. .validate() / .describe() mirror Pipeline; .http() is the session-persisted FastAPI app Pipeline(steps=..., groups=..., llm=..., traces=...) reusable facade: .run(seed) / .arun(seed) seed one artifact and return a RunResult; .answer(seed) / .aanswer(seed) return the typed answer_type; .astream(seed) yields progress events. Resources/budget/tracer are constructor defaults; result.context / .last_context are escape hatches. .override(Type, instance) replaces a typed resource (tests/fakes); lifespan= + async with manage long-lived resources; .test_client() adds an in-memory trace store; traces=True|path records every run and fills RunResult.trace_id/.trace(). .validate() runs the static contract check; .describe() returns ContractReport with seed/answer JSON Schemas; .router() / .http() are the optional FastAPI adapters; .as_tool() exposes it as a Tool/MCP tool Daemon(pipeline, *, seed_source=, interval=, run_once=, max_ticks=) interval loop over a Pipeline: seed_source(tick) may be sync/async and return None to skip; graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM, per-tick error isolation. Daemon(tick=fn) is the custom-tick form (the bundled daemon template) RunResult .context, .runs, .outcome, .latest(Type), .sources(artifact), .hash, .trace_id, .trace() RetryPolicy per-agent retry config: max_attempts, backoff, max_backoff, retry_on; a retry gets a fresh Effects slot, so only the successful patch commits run_subflow(parent, *, groups, input, output_type=, isolate=True, link=, source=, inherit_trace=True, inherit_budget=True, …) runs child agents on an isolated Context (or a parent branch), optionally links outputs to the seed, passes the parent tracer and stamps trace_metadata.parent_run_id; returns SubflowResult SubflowResult context, seed, outputs, output, run_id, parent_run_id, stats describe_contracts(groups) / ContractReport static consumes/produces/tools contract (Markdown or JSON); CLI reactifact contracts <module> [--format md\|json] validate_contracts(*, steps=, groups=, seeds=, terminal=, budget=) / ValidationReport static contract check over raw steps and/or groups (steps first, like Runtime): unknown inputs (errors), dead outputs/never-scheduled/unreachable/cycle/ambiguous_producer warnings (the last is suppressed for distinct Route cases); raise_for_errors(); CLI reactifact validate <module> (or graph --check) Wakes(False) / Scope / Unscoped / Consume / IdempotentConsume declarative (or decorator) reaction declaration; Consume.by_field for scoped events; Consume.by_base / include_subclasses=True wakes on a marker base's subclasses; IdempotentConsume(T, id_of=...) wakes only while the derived id is absent; wakes=False reads as input without waking the agent (needed only when consumes is derived from the signature); debounce=True collapses several same-generation events into one run; Annotated[T, Unscoped()] reads T across every turn instead of only the step's scope (combine with Wakes(False) for history) OnCreate / OnUpdate / OnDelete / OnStale lifecycle-specific Consume subclasses: wake only on create, update, delete or stale; OnDelete needs event/Trigger because the data is gone reactifact.consume.CorrelatedConsume fires (and feeds inputs) only for a correlation key where every require type is present and every forbid type is absent — the mechanism behind JoinConsume/AbsentConsume reactifact.consume.JoinConsume(*parts, key=…) CorrelatedConsume factory: fires once every listed type exists for the same key reactifact.consume.AbsentConsume(type, absent_type=…, key=…) CorrelatedConsume factory: fires for type only where no matching absent_type exists yet for the same key Step / @step the work unit (also scope= / Step(..., scope=...), produces=() + deletes=(T,) for side-effect-only steps): class run(...) gets typed inputs + effects: Effects; function @step gets typed inputs (or the legacy call: StepCall) and uses call.effects when it needs the effect slot. consumes declares inputs/triggers, produces the allowed create types; when consumes is explicit, typed artifact params missing from it are added as read-only inputs (wakes=False); return a model for create-sugar. Annotated[T, When(...)]/Consume.by_* select conditions; put extra creates in the same tuple (produces=(Primary, Extra)). timeout= is a hard per-step deadline; retry=, priority=, concurrency_limit= and name= are copied into the implicit group. Return Emit(model, id=..., links=(...)) when the id/provenance must be explicit, Ensure(...) for an idempotent create, or Edit/Drop/Relate for a single mutation. Human / Outbox injected non-data collaborators: human.ask/resume (HITL, PendingQuestion) and outbox.act (outbound intent, PendingAction); the old Effects.ask/resume/act were removed in 0.23 Progress injected ephemeral progress channel: progress(message, kind="status", **data) publishes a ProgressEvent immediately (a thin view over Context.announce, never committed). A step that only announces and then calls an LLM/tools needs no Context; class steps can use self.progress(...) Emit / Ensure / Edit / Drop / Relate return-style change instructions: create with explicit id/links, idempotent create (by id or source), update fields, delete, link — compiled into the same atomic patch. Emit with an existing id refreshes it (upsert); Ensure skips when it exists Trigger secondary (non-artifact) enter condition for a step; context_condition(artifact, context) for conditions that need other artifacts (joins/correlation); debounce hint consumed by Runtime StructuredGenerateAgent declarative LLM→schema→artifact agent (schema is required; build_prompt, fallback); stores a stable result id per trigger LLMAgent blocking LLM+tools loop (system, tools, max_steps, deferred_tool_groups); explicit steps= merge with the internal tool step HITLLMAgent LLM+tools loop that can pause for human answers (max_asks, resume reporting); explicit steps= merge with the internal tool step ToolUse, NativeToolUse, ToolUseHITL the tool-loop step: mode="json" | "native" | "auto"; native uses run_tool_loop/provider tool calls + textual fallback, auto falls back to JSON. ToolUse declares ToolAnswer; ToolUseHITL declares ToolAnswer/Observation/PendingQuestion and waits for a human answer. A subclass can use self.progress(...) and return Emit/Ensure (the base returns Any) DeferredToolGroup (reactifact.tools.use) a tool group whose schemas stay out of the prompt until ToolUse's built-in load_tools tool requests it (LLMAgent/ToolUse only, not the HITL variant) Inject explicit Annotated[T, Inject()] marker for an injected tool parameter (useful when a plain class would be ambiguous); Depends is a FastAPI-style alias Tool, FunctionTool, tool, ToolOutput, ToolError tool abstraction and registration; @tool(progress="Looking at {service}") gives the tool loop a localized status template; Tool.execute is instrumented once (trace ToolRun + hooks + record/replay) for both direct calls and execute_tool; @tool(retry=RetryPolicy(...), timeout=...) retries one call; a plain-class parameter is injected from RuntimeResources (not in the schema); a pydantic return type fills ToolOutput.data; ToolOutput.failed(ToolError(code=, message=, retryable=)) gives a typed failure while ToolOutput.error stays a plain string ToolAnswer, Observation tool results and model observations (loop protocol) PendingQuestion HITL primitive: a paused ask waiting for a human answer, resumed via human.resume(...); optional resolution_schema, typed resolution_data, helpers approved() / answer_text() Effects.update(artifact, *, expected_version=…, **fields) field-bump of an existing artifact; expected_version= opts into optimistic concurrency (ArtifactConflict instead of last-write-wins) PendingAction the recorded outbound side effect (kind, idempotency_key, payload, status, attempts); performed once by Runtime(dispatcher=...), then dispatched / failed (retry_action re-arms)

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text: Symbol Role Runtime wakes agents on events; run / arun / astream (each takes request=Mapping); astream_events(stream_mode=...) yields typed RunEvents; budget & concurrency; isolate_errors=True + on_agent_error(agent, event, exc) to keep one agent's exception from aborting the whole run (default: propagates, §69); dispatcher=async (context, action) drains the PendingAction outbox after each commit (once per stable id, keeping the turn alive until it is empty); on_dispatch_error(action, exc) fires when the dispatcher raises (the action is marked failed and the exception propagates); flush_pending_actions() drains without a generation (e.g. after merge()); Budget.max_seconds is a hard turn deadline (cancels the generation in flight) Runtime.request_stop() / await ashutdown(timeout=…) / in_flight graceful shutdown: stop at the next generation boundary (RunOutcome.STOPPED; the current generation still commits); ashutdown waits, force-cancelling after timeout reactifact.runtime.active_runs() / cancel_run(run_id) read-only snapshots of the process's in-flight turns (RunInfo) and targeted cancel — readiness/ops, in-process only StepCall.request the turn's request mapping inside a step (Runtime.arun(request=…) / Chat.stream(request=…)); empty when none was set Budget, RunOutcome, RunStats, BudgetTracker run limits (max_runs/max_iterations/max_seconds/max_tool_calls/max_tokens/max_cost) and the final outcome/usage stats (RunOutcome includes budget_time_exceeded and stopped). Token/cost limits count LLM usage without a tracer; cost needs an injected Pricer (reactifact.pricing) Event, EventType the wire format of "something changed" — ARTIFACT_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED/STALE EventHub, ProgressEvent progress/announce channel consumed by web UIs RunEvent (reactifact.streaming) typed events from Runtime.astream_events: RunStart/GenerationStart/AgentStart/AgentRetry/AgentEnd/ToolStart/ToolEnd/ArtifactWrite/Values/LLMDelta/CustomEvent/RunEnd/RunFailed; modes custom/updates/values/debug/messages Scheduler filter → rank → LLM tie-break agent-selection policy, callable from the runtime each iteration (see design notes) uncertainty_policy(...) builds the built-in hybrid Scheduler (filter → rank → LLM tie-break → top-k)

docs.title: Logging (reactifact.logging)
docs.text: Symbol Role configure_logging(level="INFO", *, json=False, stream=None) turn on correlated structured logs under reactifact.* — silent until called; json=True → one JSON object per line get_logger(name) a logger that injects the turn's correlation fields (run_id/session_id/generation/agent/request_id) into every record bind(**fields) add app correlation fields for a block (tenant, user, …)

docs.title: Chat layer (reactifact.chat + reactifact.web)
docs.text: Symbol Role ChatReply declarative terminal reply: ChatReply(Answer, field="query_id", render=..., extra=..., empty=...); Chat(reply=ChatReply(...)) avoids a hand-written reply(ctx, msg_id) and can share extra with Transcript.state ChatAssistant the low-level engine behind Chat: sessions + turn loop + history in one handle (stream/invoke/history); hooks: groups, user_message, reply, session_state; dispatcher=/on_dispatch_error= pass through to Runtime (outbox side effects from a chat turn) ChatMemory optional bounded memory for Chat/ChatAssistant; ChatMemory.from_transcript(transcript, ...) binds every message type, each field independent: keep (prune the raw thread), summarize+summary_type (growing digest), compact_commits (Context.compact — bounds history without touching artifacts); message_types=[UserQuery, Answer] (or a marker base) bounds a heterogeneous thread ChatEvent one transport-neutral frame; kind is a closed Literal["session","status","message"], so the schema is introspectable run_message(runtime, text, *, user_message, reply) the turn building block: create input → stream statuses → terminal reply default_session_state(ctx, user_message) generic history reader (any artifact with .text), plus the latest pending question as a waiting: true assistant message reactifact.contracts.web.create_contracts_router(groups, *, prefix=, title=, username=, password=) opt-in FastAPI router: /contracts HTML, /api/contracts JSON, /contracts.md Markdown; groups may be a zero-arg factory install_error_handlers(app, *, extra=…) maps AuthorizationError/GuardrailViolation/QuotaExceeded/MergeConflict to JSON HTTP responses (403/422/429/409) with {"error": {"code", "message", "request_id", "trace_id"}, "detail"}; extra overrides/adds mappings. create_*_app installs it together with install_request_id. install_request_id(app) middleware assigning X-Request-ID (and request.state.request_id) to every response; error envelopes reuse it and X-Reactifact-Run-Id when available create_chat_router(assistant, *, event_names=…, forward_kinds=…, payload_shaper=…, done_event=…, request_factory=…) FastAPI APIRouter for the SSE contract (/api/chat/stream, /api/runs/{id}, /api/health) — needs the web extra. The wire vocabulary is configurable (rename kinds, filter, reshape payloads, emit a terminal frame); request_factory(request) builds the per-turn request= mapping from the FastAPI Request (identity/ACL-aware turns); the event schema is published in the route's OpenAPI responses create_pipeline_router(pipeline, *, prefix=, routes_override=, request_factory=, max_iterations=, with_health=) FastAPI APIRouter for a typed Pipeline: POST /run (body seed_type, response answer_type), POST /stream (SSE progress…done/error), GET /health; FastAPI derives validation/OpenAPI//docs from the pipeline's models. PipelineRoutes overrides the paths create_chat_app(chat, *, prefix="/api", routes=, traces=, contracts=True, dependencies=, validate=True) ready FastAPI app for a Chat: sessions, history, clear, SSE, contracts and traces. ChatRoutes can expose the DEVOPS-style /chat, /chat/stream, /chat/history, /chat/clear create_http_app(pipeline, *, title=, version=, prefix=, traces=, contracts=True, dependencies=, request_factory=, validate=True, gzip=True) ready FastAPI app: pipeline router + contracts page + trace dashboard + error handlers; validate=True fails at startup on a broken contract; dependencies= applies to every router reactifact.web.sse(event, data) one SSE frame

docs.title: Visualization (reactifact.viz + python -m reactifact)
docs.text: Symbol Role blueprint(agents) static map of consumes/produces as Mermaid flowchart context_to_mermaid(context) live provenance graph of a context (artifacts + relations) trace_to_mermaid(trace) one run as a Mermaid sequenceDiagram python -m reactifact graph\|context\|trace CLI printing the diagrams to stdout reactifact new agent / new app / dev / doctor CLI: one-file minimal Pipeline / bundled FastAPI chat template / run an ASGI app with reload and contracts+traces URLs / check app settings and boundaries reactifact run / trace CLI: run a Pipeline and record .reactifact/traces.db by default (--no-trace skips), then render the latest trace without arguing the path reactifact daemon <pipeline> --seed func CLI: run a Pipeline on --interval; --run-once, --max-ticks, --trace/--no-trace trace_provenance_to_mermaid(trace, *, max_nodes=, max_edges=) a run's evidence graph (written artifacts + patch.link edges); long ids are shortened and the dashboard caps nodes/edges

docs.title: Replay (reactifact.replay, §55)
docs.text: Symbol Role ReplayLLM(recording, mode="record"\|"replay", inner=…) records every LLM call to JSONL, or replays them exactly; ReplayMiss on divergence RecordingToolRecorder / ReplayToolRecorder JSONL record/replay for tool calls (name + exact args + output/exception), covering direct tool.execute and execute_tool; ReplayMiss on an unrecorded call ReplayMiss a replaying call did not match the recording Runtime.replay_run(llm_recording=, tool_recording=, model=, save=False) temporarily installs the replay wrappers, runs a normal turn, restores resources; save=False detaches the session verify_run(build, *, recording=None, repeat=2) runs build(resources) -> Context repeat times under a recorded model and strict ids (counter_ids), returns a ReproReport; ok is False when the context_hash differs (real nondeterminism) counter_ids() a deterministic id_factory (Model:0000, Model:0001, …) for RuntimeResources(id_factory=…) — makes artifacts created without an explicit id reproducible replay_context(store, session_id, version=None) reconstructs a saved session's state at a commit replay_summary(context) compact state summary for the replay CLI — includes dispatched_actions / pending_actions / failed_actions (replay never re-sends them)

docs.title: Branching (reactifact.context + reactifact.branching, §39-§40)
docs.text: Symbol Role Context.branch(name="") forks an isolated copy; records the base snapshot for three-way merge Context.merge(other, message=…, policies=…) atomic three-way merge; MergeConflict on diverged artifacts unless a per-type MergePolicy resolves them MergeConflict raised when both sides changed an artifact differently since the fork MergePolicy (reactifact.branching) (target_data, other_data) -> merged_data callable passed per model type to Context.merge; default stays fail-loud BranchStore(KVBackend) persists branches as branch:<session>:<name> over a KV backend python -m reactifact branch … CLI: list / save / merge

docs.title: Evaluation (reactifact.eval, §56)
docs.text: Symbol Role run_suite(cases, metrics) / run_case(case, metrics) execute cases and score the final contexts EvalCase / EvalResult / EvalReport / Metric case/score/report structures (overall(), aggregate(), passed(), render(), to_dict()) core_metrics the four non-generative metrics (answer/provenance/evidence/claim) answer_coverage() · calculation_correctness(values=…) · source_coverage() · confidence_calibration() ground-truth factories (skip when expected is missing) Dataset / Example versioned examples (from_file/from_list, .json/.jsonl, content-hash version) evaluate(dataset, target, evaluators, *, extract=…, summary=…, max_concurrency=…, on_result=…) / aevaluate run a target over every example and score it; target returns a Context, ScenarioResult, outputs mapping or RunResult; on_result(result) streams each scored EvalResult (completion order when concurrent) ResultCallback Callable[[EvalResult], None] type alias for the on_result progress hook from_metric(name, metric_fn) wrap a scoring metric into an Evaluator trajectory_match(mode, *, steps=…, reference_key=…) match a run's path (strict/unordered/subset/superset) over agents/events/reads/writes llm_judge(llm, *, instructions, …) · judge_correctness · judge_relevance · judge_faithfulness LLM-as-judge evaluators (continuous/choices/include_reference) summary_pass_rate(threshold) / summary_mean(key) · assert_eval(report, …) suite-level aggregators and the CI gate OnlineEvaluator(store, config, metrics=, on_report=) · online_evaluate(store, config, metrics=) · OnlineEvalConfig score live runs sampled from a TraceStore; run_once() / run_forever(interval) trace_source() · context_source(run_fn) · output_present(key) · no_errors() what to score from a run: the trace itself, a rehydrated Context, its outputs, its spans create_online_eval_router(evaluator) FastAPI router: POST /api/evals/run, GET /api/evals/report, GET /api/evals/summary python -m reactifact eval <traces.db> CLI: online-evaluate runs (tags the results, --evaluators trace\|judge\|all) python -m reactifact check <pipeline> CLI gate: contracts + @scenario modules + a Dataset eval (--scenarios, --evals, --gate, --overall)

docs.title: Structured output
docs.text: Symbol Role structured_llm(llm, schema, *, system, user, attempts=…, validate=…, repair=…, prompt_hash=…, on_error=…) / llm.structured(...) one structured call; None on honest failure; validate(model)->bool adds a domain-rule check retried like a parse failure, repair(invalid_or_None, last_reply)->str supplies the retry instruction; on_error(reason, exc) ("no_provider"|"provider_error"|"parse_error"|"validation_error") to distinguish why, without changing the None contract json_schema_llm(llm, json_schema, *, user, validate=…, repair=…, …) / llm.structured_json(...) structured output against your own JSON Schema (dict or JSON string), returns a plain dict; same validate/repair retry hooks as structured_llm StructuredLLM(schema, *, system=…, attempts=…, on_error=…) reusable instance; .call(llm, user) llm_reply(llm, *, system, user, attempts=…, on_error=…) / llm.reply(...) plain-text completion → str or None (single-text schema under the hood) parse_structured lenient JSON→model parser used internally

docs.title: Prompts (reactifact.prompts, §68)
docs.text: Symbol Role PromptTemplate(template, *, defaults=…) strict {var} rendering: declared variables/required_variables, KeyError on missing vars, model-attribute fields ({question.text}), .partial(**defaults) for variants; identifier-shaped placeholders only — a literal JSON {"name": …} / {} in the prompt is left verbatim, no escaping. To put a placeholder inside a JSON object, double the object's outer braces: {{"answer": "{answer}"}}. Unknown !conversions and nested format specs are rejected; .hash covers the template and its defaults MessagesPrompt([(role, template), …], *, defaults=…) renders a chat sequence to list[Message]; rows may be strings or reusable PromptTemplates, defaults is shared fallback (row defaults win); .hash covers all rows and their defaults PromptSequence([part, …], *, separator="\n\n", defaults=…) composes several string/PromptTemplate sections into one text; empty sections are skipped, .required_variables/.hash cover the ordered parts and separator PromptPair(system, user, *, defaults=…) reusable system/user pair (strings, PromptTemplate or PromptSequence); .render(...) returns RenderedPrompt with .system/.user/.prompt_hash, .as_kwargs() feeds structured_llm/llm_reply

docs.title: Sources (reactifact.sources)
docs.text: Symbol Role Source ABC: asearch(query, limit) → list[SourceRef] SourceRef the shared atomic search result (ranked, scoped, stable id) FileSystemSource keyword search over local files CSVSource deterministic catalog/table search WebSource discovery + lazy remote document resolution

docs.title: Providers (reactifact.providers)
docs.text:
Every provider lazily creates its httpx.AsyncClient and rebinds it to the current event loop, so one provider instance stays usable across repeated asyncio.run(...) and per-test loops (no RuntimeError: Event loop is closed); aclose() closes the client for the running loop. The same applies to WebSource and the OTLP/Langfuse sinks.

docs.title: Branching & merge (§39-§40)
docs.text:
Live walkthrough: examples/forklab — a deterministic two-strategy fork → merge → evaluate demo, with a --conflict flag showing an explicit conflict and a policy resolving it.

State, not orchestration: a fork is an independent copy of the context for exploring an alternative state — the hypotheses of §39 are forks, not paths in an execution graph.

docs.title: Fork
docs.text:
from reactifact import Context, RuntimeResources

base = Context(resources=RuntimeResources())
base.create(Note(text="v1"), id="note:1")

hypothesis_a = base.branch(name="hypothesis-a")
hypothesis_b = base.branch(name="hypothesis-b")

# both are fully isolated from now on
hypothesis_a.create(...)
hypothesis_b.create(...)

branch() deep-copies the state and records a snapshot of the base, so a later merge of two fork-mates can detect divergence three-way. The branch shares resources with the parent but diverges in every artifact/relation.

docs.title: Merge — explicit conflicts, never a silent choice (§40)
docs.text:
hypothesis_a.merge(hypothesis_b)

Three-way merge against the shared fork base. For each artifact present in base/self/other:

Case Result self == other no-op self == base (only the other moved it) adopt other other == base (only self moved it) keep self otherwise (both diverged differently) MergeConflict, nothing applied

Merging is atomic: a single conflicting artifact aborts the whole merge, so no partial state is ever left behind. A merge that succeeds is logged as a merge commit. Deletions participate too — one side deleting an artifact the other side edited is a conflict; a clean delete propagates.

from reactifact import MergeConflict

try:
    hypothesis_a.merge(hypothesis_b)
except MergeConflict as exc:
    print(exc.conflicts)     # e.g. ["note:1 diverged since the fork (self=changed, other=changed)"]

The conflict list is the input for a verifier/merge policy — the framework does not choose (§40). When a type has a deterministic resolution, opt in per type:

left.merge(
    right,
    policies={Note: lambda a, b: Note(text=f"{a.text}\n{b.text}")},
)

A policy receives the target and incoming data and must return the same model type; without one, the merge stays fail-loud. Policies are explicit and auditable — the merge commit records the resolved value.

docs.title: Optimistic writes, not last-write-wins
docs.text:
Parallel agents in one generation share a snapshot; a plain context.update would silently keep the last write. Mark the version you read instead:

effects.update(note, expected_version=note.version, text="new")
# raises ArtifactConflict if another writer moved `note`

The runtime validates every expected_version in a generation before applying any patch, so a conflict leaves the generation untouched. Re-run the turn (or let a RetryPolicy handle the error, if you model it as one) and the agent reads the new version.

docs.title: Persistence: BranchStore on top of the KV backend
docs.text:
Branches survive restarts as named keys over the same KV backend — no new storage, the semantics live in Context operations:

from reactifact.branching import BranchStore
from reactifact.checkpoints import SQLiteKVBackend

store = BranchStore(SQLiteKVBackend("sessions.sqlite3"))
await store.save_branch(hypothesis_a, session_id="demo", name="hypothesis-a")
restored = await store.load_branch("demo", "hypothesis-a")
restored.merge(await store.load_branch("demo", "hypothesis-b"))   # base survives too

The fork base snapshot is serialized with the context, so merge keeps its conflict detection after a reload. On SQLite/Postgres, BranchStore uses the same snapshot + append-only commit log as SessionStore (per branch key), with the same compact_every bound.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
python -m reactifact branch sessions.sqlite3 demo list
python -m reactifact branch sessions.sqlite3 demo save hypothesis-a
python -m reactifact branch sessions.sqlite3 demo merge --into a --source b --as merged

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text: Situation Approach An artifact moves through phase states StatusMachine + a verification step A workflow needs to roll back on user edits stage guard + downstream resets Alternative states to explore & compare branch() + merge() (§39-§40) "Which of these did the model pick?" parse + guard (like PickStage)

docs.title: Multi-turn & chat
docs.text: A conversation is just state that persists across turns: the app enters a user message, agents react, the reply is read back, and the whole Context is kept under a session_id so the next turn — and the next process — sees it. This page maps the multi-turn pieces (and the LangGraph equivalents) to reactifact.

docs.title: If you know LangGraph
docs.text:
LangGraph reactifact thread_id + checkpointer session_id + SessionStore (FileKVBackend / SQLiteKVBackend / PostgreSQLKVBackend) MessagesState + add_messages reducer Conversation / ConversationMessage (recipes.conversation); state is typed artifacts, versioned per change graph.invoke(input, config) Chat.stream()/invoke(), or run_message() for a custom loop interrupt() / Command(resume=…) human.ask(...) → PendingQuestion → human.resume(...) get_state_history / resume a checkpoint context.history() / context.checkout(v) / context.branch() / reactifact replay bound the transcript / summarize ChatMemory → WindowPruner / RollingDigestSummarizer; Context.compact for history store (long-term, cross-thread memory) MemoryStore recipe (namespaced facts, TTL, forget_source); SessionStore remains conversation history — see Recipes

The difference in kind: a reducer merges opaque messages, whereas reactifact keeps typed, versioned artifacts — so a turn's provenance, the ability to diff two turns, and rewind are properties of the state itself.

docs.title: The canonical chat
docs.text:
Chat owns sessions, the turn loop and history; create_chat_router mounts it as SSE on your FastAPI app. Configure it with types and hooks:

from reactifact import Chat, Consume, RuntimeResources, create_step_group
from reactifact.checkpoints import SQLiteKVBackend
from reactifact.recipes.conversation import (
    ConversationMessage, conversation_state, create_turn,
)
from reactifact.session import SessionStore

assistant = Chat(
    store=SessionStore(SQLiteKVBackend("./sessions.db")),
    groups=[create_step_group("answer", steps=[ANSWER])],
    seed_type=ConversationMessage,
    create_message=create_turn,          # record the user message as a ConversationMessage
    reply=my_reply,                      # (ctx, msg_id) -> {"reply": ...}
    session_state=conversation_state,    # how history() reconstructs the thread
    resources=lambda: RuntimeResources(llm=my_llm),
)

await assistant.invoke("what's the refund policy?", session_id="user-1")
await assistant.history(session_id="user-1")   # the thread so far

A ready-made quick.chat_agent(groups, store=…) does the same with defaults.

The facade mirrors Pipeline where it matters: Chat(traces=True|path) opens a TraceStore, trace_sample= applies the same sampling policy, lifespan= + async with chat: owns long-lived resources, and await chat.answer(...) returns the typed answer_type instead of the transport payload.

Per-request metadata in create_message. The hook may take (ctx, text), (ctx, text, session_id), or (ctx, text, session_id, request) (detected from its arity). During it ctx.request is the same mapping passed to stream(..., request=...), so a turn's category/tenant/user can be stamped onto the user artifact without a ContextVar of your own:

def create_message(ctx, text, session_id):
    return ctx.create(UserQuery(
        text=text,
        session_id=session_id,
        category=ctx.request.get("category", ""),
    )).id

await assistant.invoke("...", session_id="s1", request={"category": "helm"})

resources= may also be a plain RuntimeResources instance when you want one long-lived provider shared across sessions. Per-turn budget/deadline/token tracking and tracing wrappers are installed on a shallow copy, so concurrent turns never mutate the shared instance.

Per-request resources. A resources= factory may take (session_id, request) — the same turn mapping — to build user/tenant-scoped resources per turn instead of sharing one mutable instance:

resources=lambda session_id, request: build_resources(request.get("user"))

request= is passed through unchanged (no extra keys are injected). If a turn needs the session id, read it from the request your request_factory built or from the user artifact the chat layer creates (it carries session_id). history() is read-only and does not call the factory; a shared RuntimeResources instance is still attached for a custom session_state.

Outbound side effects. If an agent in the chat records an intent with outbox.act(...), pass dispatcher= (and optionally on_dispatch_error=) — they go straight to the Runtime the assistant builds per turn, so committed actions are delivered once, after each generation's commit, exactly as in a non-chat run:

async def dispatch(context, action):
    await send_notification(action.data.payload)

Chat(..., dispatcher=dispatch)

Without it, a recorded PendingAction stays pending (the runtime warns) until something drains it — see Durability → Outbox.

docs.title: The conversation recipe
docs.text:
ConversationMessage is a canonical role/text/turn/session_id artifact, so you stop hand-rolling Question/Answer plus a prompt builder. Conversation is generic over your own message model — any model with role/text:

from reactifact.recipes.conversation import Conversation, ConversationMessage

conv = Conversation()                 # the default model
conv = Conversation(MyMessage)        # or your own (role/text/vendor fields)

conv.create_turn(ctx, "refund policy?", session_id="s1")
# ...agents run and write the assistant message...
history = conv.transcript(ctx, window=20)   # list[providers.Message] for a prompt

transcript renders the thread to provider Messages (oldest first, window keeps the last N, 0 means empty); conversation_state is the session_state= history payload; turn numbers come from the max recorded turn, so pruning never restarts them. add/create_turn are app-side hooks; inside a Step use conv.add_effect(effects, ...) or return an Emit.

Most real apps have separate types for the two sides (Question + FinalResponse, UserMsg + ChatReply) with a correlation key and a non-text assistant payload. For those, use the read-only Transcript + MessageSpec, which merges several typed turns by role and leaves the artifacts untouched — the shape the repair/devops/knowledge examples use (each defining a Transcript([...]) as its session_state=):

from reactifact.recipes.conversation import MessageSpec, Transcript

view = Transcript([
    MessageSpec(Question, "user"),
    MessageSpec(FinalResponse, "assistant", render=render_answer),  # contract JSON → prose
])
history = view.messages(ctx, window=20)      # list[providers.Message]
# Chat(..., session_state=view.state)

view.entries(ctx) is the lower-level form: it returns the ordered TranscriptEntry(spec, artifact) pairs, so a step that needs the artifacts themselves (ids, versions, metadata) does not have to re-scan Context.

docs.title: Bounded memory
docs.text:
A conversation grows forever unless you bound it. ChatMemory on Chat wires the memory recipes for you:

from reactifact import Chat
from reactifact.chat import ChatMemory

assistant = Chat(
    ...,
    memory=ChatMemory(
        message_type=ConversationMessage,
        # message_types=[UserQuery, Answer],  # heterogeneous thread / marker base
        keep=20,                 # keep the last 20 raw messages (WindowPruner)
        # or, to condense instead of dropping:
        # summarize=my_summarize,      # (ctx, previous_digest, stale) -> str | None
        # summary_type=Summary,        # the digest artifact (needs a `text` field,
        # build_summary=lambda t: Summary(text=t),   # or pass a builder)
        compact_commits=200,     # also bound the commit log (Context.compact)
    ),
)

Use one shape or the other, not both: pruning keeps the raw window; summarizing folds what falls out of it into a growing digest and deletes the source messages. compact_commits is orthogonal — it bounds the history (see Durability & resume), not the working set, and needs no message_type, so ChatMemory(compact_commits=…) is a complete policy on its own (the safe choice when messages are correlated/typed rather than a plain role/text log, e.g. separate Question/Answer artifact types).

When the thread really is more than one artifact type, pass message_types=[UserQuery, Answer] — or a marker base (ChatMessage) whose concrete types inherit it. The memory agent wakes on every listed type (and, for a marker base, on its subclasses), so one window bounds the whole thread; message_type also accepts a sequence for the same effect.

docs.title: Three kinds of memory
docs.text:
These are different lifecycles, not alternatives:

What Where it lives Lifetime Use it for Conversation history SessionStore + the session Context per session_id, until deleted continue/replay a thread; history() Working window ChatMemory (WindowPruner / RollingDigestSummarizer), Context.compact the live Context bound the prompt/history without growing forever Long-term facts MemoryStore (recipes) per namespace (user:<id>), TTL/forget_source preferences and learned facts across sessions Operational traces TraceStore retention policy debugging/quality monitoring, not user memory

SessionStore is what happened in this conversation; MemoryStore is what the agent should remember about this user; ChatMemory is how much of the transcript to keep in the prompt. Keep them separate.

docs.title: Human-in-the-loop turns
docs.text:
A turn can pause for a human without any special machinery — asking is just an effect, and the answer is just another patch:

# inside a step
human.ask("Approve this estimate?", kind="approval")
# later, from your API, when the human answers:
ctx.resume(question_id, "approved")   # emits an update → agents react

The pending question is state, so it survives a restart like everything else — a client can come back with the answer on a later turn. See the devops and repair examples.

docs.title: Rewind and resume
docs.text:
• Continue an interrupted run: reopen the session and arun() — pending triggers are restored (Durability & resume).
  • Rewind to an earlier point: context.checkout(version) (refused below a compaction baseline) or context.branch() to explore an alternative without touching the original.
  • Inspect a turn: context.diff(v1, v2) shows exactly what changed, reactifact replay reconstructs why.

docs.text:

docs.title: reactifact vs. LangGraph / CrewAI / plain function calls
docs.text: This page is a comparison, not a pitch. reactifact is pre-1.0 (0.25.1), the ecosystem is one maintainer, and there is no hosted platform, no managed tracing SaaS, no marketplace of pre-built agents. If any of those are what you need today, the honest answer is: use LangGraph or CrewAI, they're mature and well-supported. Read on if the comparison below still tips your way.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: LangGraph CrewAI reactifact Primary abstraction explicit state graph (nodes + edges) role-based crew of agents typed artifacts + reactive agents Control flow you draw it mostly fixed (sequential/hierarchical) derived from state changes State a shared, loosely-typed dict/TypedDict task outputs passed along versioned, typed, immutable-per-version artifacts "Why did it say that?" requires manual logging/checkpoint inspection not tracked by default provenance graph (supported_by/derived_from/…) built in Numbers/calculations the LLM computes unless you write a tool same recipes push calculation into deterministic code, not the model Rollback / branching checkpointer + manual replay logic not built in context.branch(), three-way merge(), deterministic replay Maturity / ecosystem high — used in production widely high — large community pre-1.0, one maintainer, small examples set Managed hosting LangGraph Platform CrewAI Enterprise none MCP via LangChain adapters via CrewAI adapters client + server built in (reactifact.mcp, mcp extra)

docs.title: Where reactifact is not the right choice
docs.text:
Being upfront about this matters more than the feature table:

  • You have a genuinely fixed pipeline. If the steps are always A → B → C with no branching by data, a graph framework (or a plain function) is less ceremony than modeling artifacts and consumes/produces.
  • You need a managed platform today — hosted execution, a UI for non-engineers, an enterprise support contract. reactifact is a library; there is no SaaS behind it.
  • You need a large pre-built agent/tool ecosystem. LangGraph and CrewAI both have more third-party integrations, more Stack Overflow answers, more production war stories. reactifact's Source abstraction is intentionally small (filesystem, CSV, web); vector retrieval lives in the optional reactifact.knowledge layer (KnowledgePipeline + IndexSource). reactifact.mcp (docs) reaches any MCP server as a Tool, which narrows this for tool-calling specifically, but doesn't touch Source/retrieval integrations.
  • Your team already has deep LangGraph investment. Rewriting a working system for architectural purity is rarely worth it. reactifact is a better fit for a new agent, not necessarily a migration target for an old one.

docs.title: 1. The state model: a dict vs. typed, versioned artifacts
docs.text:
LangGraph's state is a shared dict (or TypedDict) that every node can read and mutate. That's flexible, but it means "what shape does the state have right now" is a runtime fact, not something the type checker can verify, and "who last touched this field" is not tracked unless you add it yourself.

reactifact artifacts are pydantic models. Every artifact has a type, an id, a version, and a created_at. Nothing is deleted-and-overwritten in place — an Update produces a new version, so context.diff(v1, v2) is a real, inspectable operation, not something you have to reconstruct from logs.

docs.title: 2. Control flow: drawn graph vs. reactive dispatch
docs.text:
A LangGraph graph is the orchestration: you write add_edge, add_conditional_edges, you decide by hand which node can follow which. That's the right model when there genuinely is one path. It stops being the right model once the paths multiply — a real knowledge-agent question ("why did infra costs jump in Q2?") might need Confluence and GitLab and a CSV calculation and human confirmation, and the next question needs a different subset. Encoding every combination as graph edges turns into a combinatorial wiring exercise.

reactifact agents declare consumes/produces — what artifact types they react to and what they can create. The runtime derives execution from which artifacts actually exist, not from a pre-declared path. Two agents that have never heard of each other compose correctly as long as one produces what the other consumes. viz.blueprint() renders that static consumes/produces declaration map; it is not an execution graph you keep in sync by hand — see Why reactifact for the full argument.

docs.title: 3. Provenance: bolt-on vs. built-in
docs.text:
"Why did the agent answer this?" in LangGraph/CrewAI usually means reading logs, message history, or a custom trace you added yourself. There's no first-class notion of "this Answer artifact is derived from this Evidence, which was extracted from this Doc."

In reactifact, effects.create(...).link("supported_by", evidence) is a normal part of writing a step, and the resulting graph is queryable: context.related(answer.id, "supported_by"), or rendered as a Mermaid graph via context_to_mermaid(). This isn't a logging add-on — it's the same mechanism the runtime uses to decide what to re-run after a rollback.

docs.title: 4. Determinism: the model computes vs. the model reasons
docs.text:
Ask an LLM to compute sum(gpu_cost) / sum(total_cost) inline in a chat completion and it will confidently produce a number that is sometimes wrong — this is not a prompting problem, it's what generative token-by-token math does. Both LangGraph and CrewAI leave this entirely up to you (write a tool, remember to call it, remember to trust its output over the model's).

reactifact's design bias — not a hard rule — is that a Step doing arithmetic over structured data (a CSV, a query result) should compute it in plain Python and hand the LLM the result to explain, not the raw numbers to guess from. The knowledge example does exactly this: the LLM writes the prose, calc.py does the arithmetic.

docs.title: 5. Rollback and branching: checkpointer vs. git-like context
docs.text: LangGraph has checkpointers for persistence and time-travel through checkpoint history. reactifact's Context is versioned more literally: you can context.branch() to fork a parallel exploration, run different agents on each fork, and three-way merge() them back — see Branching and the forklab example, which runs two strategies on their own forks and merges the result.

docs.title: If you're evaluating both
docs.text: A reasonable trial: take one agent from your LangGraph/CrewAI project that does non-trivial branching (not a fixed 3-step pipeline) and port just that one to reactifact. If the artifact model and reactive dispatch make that agent's logic shorter and more honest about failure (no silent wrong-number hallucination, real "why" for its answer), the rest of the system is probably worth porting too. If it mostly adds ceremony for a genuinely linear flow, that agent was never the graph-heavy case reactifact is built for.

docs.title: Starting from scratch (nothing to port)
docs.text:
The trial above assumes an existing graph to compare against. If you don't have one, the equivalent test doesn't need a pre-existing project — it needs a third thing to wire in after the fact:

  1. Pick a question that genuinely needs two independent things combined (a CSV number and a doc lookup, say — not a fixed A→B pipeline).
  2. Write it as two Steps that each declare only what they consume/ produce — the front-page example's two-agent snippet (find_evidence/answer) is the shape. Neither should import or reference the other by name.
  3. Now add a third agent for a follow-up question that needs a different subset of the same data — without touching the first two agents' code.

If step 3 composes cleanly, that's the actual claim on this page, not a marketing line — open a discussion with what you built (or where it didn't compose the way this page claims); that's a faster way to get a straight answer than reading more docs, and it's exactly the kind of report that makes this comparison more honest over time.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: The full design rationale lives in constitution.md. This page is the operative overview: the six building blocks and how they interact.

docs.title: 1. Context
docs.text:
Context is the versioned working state. Like git, it keeps a history of commits, each commit being the result of applying one or more patches.

from reactifact import Context, RuntimeResources
from reactifact.sources import FileSystemSource

ctx = Context(
    resources=RuntimeResources(
        sources={"docs": FileSystemSource("./docs")},
    )
)

Key capabilities:

Capability Purpose create / update / delete encode intent (delegated per-run to agents) list_artifacts(Model) query the current state by artifact type view((M1, M2), condition=…) query a type join for decisions/chat memory related(artifact_id, relation) walk the provenance graph announce(message, kind=…) emit a progress/status event to the UI diff / checkout / merge inspect or unwind history; merge forks

Context.resources carries what is not state: providers (the LLM, an embedder), sources, and arbitrary app resources (a price catalog, an image directory). Agents read them; they never persist them.

docs.title: 2. Artifact
docs.text:
An Artifact is an immutable handle (id, version, data, content_hash, …) where data is a pydantic model. Artifacts are first-class objects, not string blobs. Every revision lives in the context's ArtifactStore; reads via Context.artifact_version/version_history/find_versions, while Artifact.at/history are compatibility bridges. Mutation is Context.update (or effects), never mutating artifact.data in place — the content hash is the identity.

class Evidence(BaseModel):
    query_id: str
    source: str
    text: str
    score: float

Rules of thumb:

  • Every artifact has a stable id. Prefer stable ids over random ones (answer:{query_id}, ref:{stable_id}:{owner}) — idempotency and provenance linking become trivial.
  • query_id is the conventional owner key when many artifacts belong to one workflow turn (a question, a research turn). Recipes and examples rely on it.
  • Artifacts are immutable as data; change is expressed through patches that create new versions.

docs.title: 3. Effects & Patch
docs.text:
The authoring surface is the effects slot (see The step contract, §24): a step writes create/update/delete/link/upsert and returns None. A class-style step declares effects: Effects in run(); a @step function uses call.effects. The runtime compiles the effect set into one atomic Patch — its compiled transport.

from reactifact import Effects

async def run(self, effects: Effects) -> None:
    answer = effects.create(Answer(query_id=qid, text=text), id="answer:q1")
    answer.link("supported_by", evidence_id)
    effects.update(some_artifact, status="answered")
    return None

The compiled operations (reactifact.operations):

Op Meaning Create add an artifact (optionally with a stable id) Update / update_fields a new revision of an artifact Delete remove an artifact Link connect source →rel→ target (provenance) Unlink remove a relation

Patch (the container) is built by the runtime and by the StepGroup.run escape hatch; effects compose within one produce, so nothing is applied until the runtime compiles — atomicity is structural (§41).

HITL is an human.ask(...) → PendingQuestion, answered via human.resume(...) (see patterns).

docs.title: 4. StepGroup (optional container)
docs.text:
Steps are the model. Runtime(ctx, steps=[...]) wraps each step in an implicit group of one, so the common case needs no container at all. A StepGroup is the optional container for steps that must share something operational: one trigger, retry policy, timeout, priority, concurrency limit, or one atomic commit. Runtime accepts steps= and groups= together (steps first).

from reactifact import StepGroup

class RepairFlow(StepGroup):
    name = "repair_flow"
    steps = [
        CollectStage(), PickStage(), PlanStage(),
        EstimateStage(), ApprovalStage(), AssistantStage(),
    ]
  • steps — the unit-of-work instances. A step's consumes both feeds its typed inputs and decides which events can run it; produces is the allowed create set. Put the primary output first and extra create-only types in the same tuple: produces = (Primary, Extra); the old also_creates= spelling was removed in 0.23, so extra types belong in produces itself.
  • StepGroup.consumes still exists for the imperative escape hatch (a group subclass overriding run(event, context) directly), but declarative code should put contracts on steps.
  • When consumes is explicit, typed artifact params missing from it are added as read-only inputs automatically; Consume(..., wakes=False) remains for an explicit list without a typed param. IdempotentConsume(T, id_of=...) wakes only while the derived target id is absent. debounce=True collapses several same-generation events into one run; Consume.by_base(Base) also wakes on subclasses. JoinConsume/AbsentConsume correlate across types — see patterns.
  • The runtime wakes groups on events, respecting budget and concurrency.

StepGroup.run(event, context) -> Patch | None remains the low-level escape hatch for hand-assembling a Patch; it is not a third everyday style. The 0.x Agent/create_agent aliases are removed in 0.24; use StepGroup/create_step_group.

docs.title: 5. Step
docs.text:
Step is where the work happens. A class step declares consumes/produces and receives typed inputs plus effects: Effects in run():

from reactifact import Artifact, Effects, Progress, Step

class EstimateStage(Step):
    consumes = (Project,)
    produces = (Project,)

    async def run(
        self,
        project_art: Artifact[Project],
        effects: Effects,
        progress: Progress,
    ) -> None:
        ...
        progress("Считаю смету…")
        effects.update(project_art, stage="estimate")

progress is optional: it publishes an ephemeral UI status (ProgressEvent) without injecting the whole Context. Use it when a step only announces and then works with an LLM, tools or domain logic. The same resolver also injects other non-model parameters from RuntimeResources, including optional ones: llm: LLMProvider | None gives the configured provider or an honest None. An explicitly registered type wins over artifact resolution, so a pydantic settings object (resources.register(Settings, Settings(...))) can be injected as a resource; unregistered pydantic models stay artifacts.

When consumes is explicit, it is the step's wake set; its typed signature is the read set. A typed artifact parameter that is not in consumes is added automatically as a read-only input (Consume(T, wakes=False)):

class PickStage(Step):
    consumes = (UserMsg,)          # only a new message wakes it

    async def run(
        self,
        user: Artifact[UserMsg],
        project: Artifact[Project],  # read-only: collected, never wakes
    ) -> Any:
        ...

project is still collected, validated and recorded as an input — it just never wakes the step on its own. If consumes is omitted, the typed signature derives both triggers and inputs; mark an individual read-only input there with Annotated[T, Wakes(False)]. Latest[T] remains an ad-hoc context query, not a declared input.

T injects the data model, while Artifact[T] injects the handle (id, version, for Edit/links). Add | None to either form when the input may be absent: Artifact[T] | None gives the handle or None, not the data model.

The function form takes one call: StepCall and uses call.effects:

@step(produces=Answer, consumes=Evidence)
async def answer(call: StepCall) -> Answer:
    return Answer(text=call.trigger.data.text)

Returning a model is create-sugar; effects.* is for updates, links, HITL and extra creates. produces validates every create type, including effect-created ones. See effects and patterns.

Convention: determinism first (§67). Eligibility is decided by the step's consumes/When selectors, not by a manual graph edge; LLM use is reserved for genuinely generative tasks and is wrapped with a schema + fallback.

docs.title: 6. Provenance
docs.text:
Every derived artifact links to what produced it. The runtime records reads and writes automatically; your code adds domain relations via patch.link:

Answer ──supported_by──► Claim ──derived_from──► Evidence ──extracted_from──► Doc

Why this matters:

  • Explainability — "show your sources" is a query over relations, not LLM memory.
  • Scoring — an answer's strength is the conjunction of its claims' confidence and their evidence support.
  • Deterministic auditing — every run trace includes the reads/writes of each agent span.

docs.title: Supporting pieces
docs.text:
• Budget / RunOutcome / RunStats — limit runs, iterations, wall-clock, tool calls, and LLM tokens/cost; on exhaustion the runtime stops and reports the outcome (RunStats carries the token/cost totals; cost needs an injected pricer).
  • Event / EventType — the wire format of "something changed"; agents are woken by artifacts' create/update events, and the announce mechanism emits status events on the way to the UI. ARTIFACT_STALE fires automatically when an artifact's recorded dependency (§43-44) gets a newer version — opt in with OnStale(Type) (or the explicit Consume(Type, event_types=[...])).
  • Trigger — secondary enter conditions for a produce (e.g. a periodic or timer-based wake), independent of the artifact consumes. context_condition is the two-artifact form (needed for joins/correlation); debounce is the hint Runtime reads to collapse repeat events into one run.
  • Session / SessionStore — durable, per-chat working memory across requests, backed by a KV checkpoint (file or SQLite); Context.compact(...) bounds a long session's history.

docs.title: Which API do I use?
docs.text: This is a ladder, not more concepts: start at the first row and only descend when the task actually needs it.

docs.title: Authoring a step
docs.text: Need Use Notes One typed transformation @step(produces=..., consumes=...) return the produced model, or use call.effects for updates/links Typed inputs, several effects, HITL class Step with run(..., effects: Effects) the full form; see Effects Hand-assembled operations / imperative agent Patch, StepGroup.run(event, context) escape hatch, not the everyday style

docs.title: Scheduling
docs.text: Need Use React to a type Consume(Type) Only one lifecycle event OnCreate(Type), OnUpdate(Type), OnDelete(Type), OnStale(Type) Conditional edge Consume.by_status(...) / Consume.by_field(...), Annotated[T, When(...)] Read without waking / latest / scoped lookup a typed param missing from explicit consumes (automatic), Annotated[T, Wakes(False)] when consumes is derived, Consume(..., wakes=False), Latest[T], Scope(...), scope= on Step/@step Cross-turn history Annotated[list[Artifact[T]], Unscoped()] / Annotated[Latest[T], Unscoped()] (add Wakes(False) for reads) Periodic/join/absent/debounced Trigger, JoinConsume, AbsentConsume, debounce=True

docs.title: Streams
docs.text: Need Use Canonical chat UI ChatEvent from Chat.stream() / create_chat_router Live UI / Studio / token deltas RunEvent from Runtime.astream_events(stream_mode=...) Simple CLI/status ProgressEvent from Runtime.astream() (legacy status stream)

docs.title: Persistence and memory
docs.text: Need Use Continue a conversation SessionStore + session_id Bound/summarize the prompt ChatMemory (WindowPruner / RollingDigestSummarizer) Remember facts across sessions MemoryStore (recipes) Inspect/rewind a turn ContextCheckpoint (context.checkpoints() / at()) Try alternative paths context.branch() + merge()

docs.title: Resource ownership
docs.text:
RuntimeResources.aclose() closes llm and embedder, plus every typed resource registered with owned=True — in reverse registration order, before the providers. Owned clients are duck-typed: an async aclose() or a sync close().

resources.register(
    ImageRenderSettings,
    ImageRenderSettings(provider=image_from_env(), out_dir=...),
    owned=True,
)
...
await resources.aclose()  # owned resources, then embedder, then llm

Everything else (sources, shared clients, MemoryStore, DB pools) is app-owned: leave owned=False (the default) and close it in your lifespan, not per turn. The distinction matters for a callable resources= factory: ChatAssistant closes that per-turn instance after every turn, so mark only what the factory itself created.

docs.title: Durability & resume
docs.text: reactifact is single-process and has no broker, but a session-backed run survives a process restart: reopen the session and keep going instead of losing the work an interrupted run had queued. This page states exactly what that guarantee is — and what it is not.

docs.title: What is persisted
docs.text:
A SessionStore persists the Context under a session_id — as one blob for FileKVBackend/InMemoryKVBackend, or as a snapshot plus an appended commit log for AppendBackend:

  • the artifacts (typed, versioned) and the relations between them;
  • the commit chain (Context.history()), so provenance and diff/ checkout/replay still work;
  • the pending trigger queue — the events no generation has dispatched yet.
