Capability Providers Image OpenAICompatImageProvider (any image API), OpenRouterImageProvider, GeminiImageProvider, gemini_image, image_from_env Embeddings OpenAICompatEmbedder, openai_embedder, mistral_embedder, openrouter_embedder, together_embedder, fireworks_embedder, qwen_embedder, nvidia_embedder, embedder_from_env Speech (TTS) OpenAICompatSpeech, openrouter_speech, speech_from_env Speech (STT) OpenAICompatTranscriber, groq_transcriber, transcriber_from_env Video SoraVideoProvider, RunwayVideoProvider, LumaVideoProvider, OpenRouterVideoProvider, video_from_env — generate()/fetch()/download() all retry (same policy as chat); poll() itself tolerates a fetch() that still fails after its own retry and keeps polling until timeout, rather than abandoning a multi-minute job over one bad network moment

Each *_from_env accepts **overrides so you can inject config in tests without setting environment variables.

docs.title: .env reference (examples)
docs.text:
Every demo ships an .env.example; a typical one for a chat model looks like:

# model selection (the *_from_env factories read these)
LLM_PROVIDER=openrouter
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-...
OPENROUTER_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-chat

# optional
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=mistral
MISTRAL_API_KEY=...
IMAGE_PROVIDER=openrouter
IMAGE_MODEL=google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
Retries. Every provider (OpenAICompatProvider/Embedder, AnthropicProvider, GeminiProvider, OpenAICompatImageProvider, OpenAICompatSpeech/ Transcriber, all four video providers) takes retry_attempts (default 3) and retries 429/5xx and transport errors with exponential backoff via reactifact.providers._retry.with_retry — 4xx (auth/bad request) never retries, since retrying a misconfiguration just delays the real error. Pass retry_attempts=1 to disable.

Failover. RouterLLM([primary, secondary, …]) calls providers in order and falls back on failure — a provider outage, a rate limit, or a missing key while another provider works. Any exception falls back by default; should_fallback= narrows it (e.g. retryable_only skips a 4xx, which would repeat everywhere). Only complete() fails over — stream() uses the first provider. An on_fallback(provider, exc) callback fires before moving on.

Exact cache. CachingLLM(provider) keys every complete() by the whole request (model, messages, temperature, …) and answers a repeat without calling the provider — no tokens, no latency; cache=KVCache(FileKVBackend(…)) makes it survive restarts. A hit is marked (raw={"reactifact_cache": "hit"}) and BudgetLLM does not charge it. Deliberately not semantic (an approximate match would answer a different question), and stream() is not cached.

from reactifact.cache import CachingLLM, KVCache
from reactifact.checkpoints import SQLiteKVBackend
from reactifact.routing import RouterLLM, retryable_only

resources.llm = CachingLLM(                     # cache outermost
    RouterLLM([openrouter_llm(), groq_llm()],   # failover in the middle
              should_fallback=retryable_only),
    cache=KVCache(SQLiteKVBackend("llm-cache.db")),
)

HTTP client lifecycle. Every provider opens an httpx.AsyncClient lazily and owns it — nothing in the runtime closes it for you. Call await resources.aclose() (RuntimeResources) yourself at real shutdown (a FastAPI lifespan, or the end of a script):

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    yield
    await resources.aclose()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

The one exception is Chat with a callable resources= (e.g. resources=lambda: build_resources()): a fresh RuntimeResources — and typically a fresh provider + HTTP client — is built on every turn, so stream() closes it after that turn itself; nothing else will ever reference that instance again. A plain (non-callable) resources= instance is left alone — it must outlive the turn.

docs.title: Temperature & max_tokens — provider defaults, per-call overrides
docs.text:
temperature and max_tokens are provider-level defaults, overridable per call. A None at both levels means the field is omitted from the request and the API applies its own default.

from reactifact.providers import openai_llm, openrouter_llm

# provider default for every request made through it
llm = openai_llm(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0.7, max_tokens=2048)

Per-call overrides win (e.g. a deterministic extractor that must not wander):

body = await structured_llm(llm, schema=AnswerBody, user=text, temperature=0.0)

Resolution order: call → provider → omit the field. The same applies to llm_reply, ToolUse, LLMAgent/HITLLMAgent (temperature/max_tokens class attributes, None = provider default), and to the image provider (n/size/quality defaults in the constructor, per-call override via generate(prompt, size=...)). Anthropic always sends max_tokens (the API requires it) — default 4096, change it in the constructor.

docs.title: Deterministic demo mode
docs.text: When no LLM is configured (llm_from_env() returns None and no fallback is set), demos switch to deterministic behavior: canned options, fallback plans, rule-based summarizing (§68). The rule is strict: a configured model that returns nothing usable is reported honestly (never silently substituted with stubs); the deterministic fallback is only for "no model at all" mode.

docs.title: Quickstart — three real applications
docs.text: The front-page example proves the idea (evidence → answer, no graph wired between the two agents) in the smallest possible shape. This page bridges the gap to something you'd actually build: three short, runnable snippets — a tool-calling agent, retrieval over your own docs, and a session-persisted chat bot — each pointing at the full, production-shaped example it's trimmed from. Every snippet on this page was run to produce the output shown; none of it is hypothetical.

docs.title: Install and scaffold with uv
docs.text:
uv init my-agent && cd my-agent
uv add reactifact                 # core + CLI; FastAPI stays optional
uv run reactifact skills install  # teach your coding agent the model

Or start from the one-file agent template (no web, no API key):

uvx reactifact new agent my-agent
cd my-agent && uv sync
uv run reactifact run main:pipeline "hello"
uv run reactifact trace

run writes .reactifact/traces.db; trace renders the latest run. Use --no-trace to skip it.

The fastest way to see the claim end to end — a computed figure, its provenance, and a reproducible context hash, with no API key and no files — is the bundled demo:

uv run reactifact demo            # ~3 seconds; --plain disables colour
uv run reactifact demo --web      # same answer, provenance, contracts + traces

It is the same three-@step shape you'll write below, and the whole source is reactifact/demo.py. --web serves it locally and opens the browser; use --no-open in a terminal you don't want to interrupt.

For a web app, either add the extra yourself or generate the template:

uv add "reactifact[web]"          # + FastAPI/uvicorn
uv run reactifact new app my-app  # or: uvx reactifact new app my-app
cd my-app && uv sync --extra dev
cp .env.example .env
uv run reactifact dev

reactifact dev starts the app with reload and prints the three URLs worth opening: the app, /contracts and /traces (when mounted). Pass app.main:create_app explicitly or use --open /contracts to open the browser.

reactifact new app copies the bundled FastAPI template (auth, sessions, SSE, traces, settings-driven budgets/LLM). The generated project owns its reactifact[web] dependency; the core package never requires FastAPI.

reactifact new daemon generates a scheduled agent loop instead: settings-driven LLM/budget, traces, graceful shutdown, and APP_RUN_ONCE=true for a one-shot smoke run.

The loop is also available as a library:

import asyncio

from reactifact import Daemon

asyncio.run(
    Daemon(
        pipeline,
        seed_source=next_tick,   # sync/async: tick index -> seed | None
        interval=60,
    ).serve()
)
# tracing is configured on the Pipeline (traces=True/path), not on Daemon

reactifact daemon app.pipeline:pipeline --seed app.seeds:next_tick --interval 60 runs the same thing from the CLI.

docs.title: Chat in a few lines
docs.text:
Chat is the typed facade over ChatAssistant: seed and reply come from the models, sessions are persisted, and streaming/history are ready.

from reactifact import Chat

chat = Chat(
    steps=[search, answer],
    store="sessions.db",
    seed_type=Question,
    answer_type=Answer,
)

reply = await chat.invoke("why is checkout down?", session_id="u1")
async for event in chat.stream("and now?", session_id="u1"):
    ...

seed_factory(text, session_id, request) supplies app metadata (a category, tenant, user); per_turn(text, session_id, request) is an async context manager for turn-scoped context vars or resource cleanup. chat.router() returns a ready FastAPI APIRouter (SSE + history), and chat.test_client() is a copy with an in-memory store and traces. A pending PendingQuestion is reported as waiting: true; with Chat(..., resume_pending=True) the next user message is its answer, so HITL needs no separate endpoint.

For a sessionful HTTP app, chat.http() adds the same paths as the DEVOPS-style API:

from reactifact.web import ChatRoutes

app = chat.http(
    routes=ChatRoutes(
        invoke="/chat",          # POST /api/chat
        stream="/chat/stream",   # POST /api/chat/stream
        history="/chat/history", # GET  /api/chat/history
        clear="/chat/clear",     # POST /api/chat/clear
        clear_method="POST",
        history_messages=True,
    )
)

/docs, /api/contracts and /api/traces are mounted too; reactifact dev serves it.

docs.title: One object: Pipeline
docs.text:
Pipeline is the short path when you already have steps: it owns the steps, resources and defaults, and builds a fresh Context + Runtime per run.

from reactifact import Pipeline

pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[compute_spend, compute_variance, answer])
result = pipeline.run(Question(text="what is the Q2 variance?"))

print(result.latest(Answer).data.text)
print(result.sources(result.latest(Answer)))
print(result.hash)

Async variants are arun(seed) and astream(seed); the low-level Context is still on result.context for branch/merge, replay and tests.

Steps can also receive resources by type, and tests can override them without rebuilding the pipeline:

@step(consumes=Question)
def answer(question: Question, llm: LLMProvider) -> Answer: ...

pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[answer], llm=default_llm)
pipeline.override(LLMProvider, FakeLLM())

For long-lived resources (HTTP clients, indexes) use a lifespan, like FastAPI:

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan():
    yield build_resources()
    await close_resources()

async with Pipeline(steps=[answer], lifespan=lifespan) as pipeline:
    result = await pipeline.arun(Question(text="..."))

Tests get an in-memory trace store and isolated overrides:

client = pipeline.test_client()
client.override(LLMProvider, FakeLLM())
result = client.run(Question(text="..."))
assert asyncio.run(client.traces.query())["total"] >= 1
client.close()

docs.title: One command: check
docs.text:
reactifact check runs the quality loop over a Pipeline: static contracts, registered scenarios and a dataset evaluation, then exits non-zero if any stage fails.

uv run reactifact check app.pipeline:pipeline \
  --scenarios app.scenarios \
  --evals evals/qa.json \
  --overall 0.8

It prints one line per stage and a final check: PASSED/FAILED gate; use --gate KEY=VALUE for a metric-specific bar. reactifact dev is the server counterpart: it starts the app and points at /contracts and /traces.

docs.title: HTTP in one line
docs.text:
The web adapter is optional; when you need HTTP, it comes from the same typed pipeline:

pipeline = Pipeline(
    steps=[extract, classify, answer],
    seed_type=Question,
    answer_type=Answer,
    traces=True,
)

app = pipeline.http()

reactifact dev main:app then serves POST /run, POST /stream, /health, interactive /docs (OpenAPI generated from Question/Answer), /contracts and /traces. Every response carries X-Request-ID; /run adds X-Reactifact-Run-Id, and domain errors use {"error": {"code", "message", "request_id", "trace_id"}}. To mount it in an existing app, use app.include_router(pipeline.router(prefix="/agent")).

docs.title: 0. The 80% on-ramp: reactifact.quick
docs.text:
Most first tasks are one of four things. reactifact.quick wires each of them in a few lines, while still building real reactive agents under the hood:

from pydantic import BaseModel
from reactifact.quick import agent, rag, tools_agent, chat_agent


class AnswerBody(BaseModel):
    text: str


# 1) one structured LLM call
qa = agent(system="Answer in one sentence.", schema=AnswerBody)
body = await qa.ask("What are the three states of water?")   # AnswerBody | None

# 2) retrieval over your own files, with provenance
r = rag({"docs": "./docs", "costs": "./costs.csv"})
answer = await r.ask("what's the total gpu cost?")           # answer.text, answer.sources

# 3) an LLM with tools (human=True → asks clarifying questions instead)
t = tools_agent("You are ops. Use the tools.", [check_status])  # a @tool (§1)
text = await t.ask("is checkout-api healthy?")

# 4) a session-persisted chat assistant (store=None → in-memory)
assistant = chat_agent(groups=[...], llm=provider)

Every entry point takes llm= — any LLMProvider (from_env(), openai_llm(...), openrouter_llm(...), …). It defaults to from_env(), so a configured .env just works; pass it explicitly to choose a model/endpoint.

This is sugar over the same primitives, not a second framework. Every object exposes the real StepGroup and the Context the run produced:

qa.agent      # the reactive StepGroup — mount it on your own Runtime
qa.context    # the artifacts/provenance of the last ask()

rag(...) links every Answer supported_by the Docs it used, and each Doc materialized_from its SourceRef — the same provenance the hand-written pipeline below builds. When the facade no longer fits, drop to Consume/Step/Effects with nothing to rewrite. See Patterns for the full model.

Prefer a notebook? — examples/quickstart.ipynb walks the same four cases, offline by default.

Bring your own artifact models — the facade is parameterized, not fixed:

r = rag(
    {"docs": "./docs"},
    doc_type=MyDoc,          # must accept text/locator/title…
    answer_type=MyAnswer,
    # …or build them yourself and say how to read a doc's body/label:
    doc_factory=lambda ctx, ref, content: MyDoc(body=content, url=ref.data.locator),
    answer_factory=lambda text, docs: MyAnswer(answer=text, citations=[d.data.url for d in docs]),
    doc_text=lambda d: d.body,
    doc_locator=lambda d: d.url,
)
qa = agent("Answer briefly.", AnswerBody, question_type=MyQuestion)  # needs a `text` field

Provenance is unaffected by the model shape: an answer is still linked supported_by the documents it used.

docs.title: 1. A tool-calling agent (with human-in-the-loop)
docs.text:
HITLLMAgent wires an LLM + a Tool list into the reactive ask/tool/answer loop for you — the model decides whether to call a tool, ask the user a clarifying question, or answer, one step at a time (§60). No manual "if missing, ask" branch anywhere in your own code:

import asyncio
from pydantic import BaseModel

from reactifact import Consume, Context, Runtime, RuntimeResources
from reactifact.llm_agent import HITLLMAgent
from reactifact.providers import from_env
from reactifact.tools import tool


class Ticket(BaseModel):
    text: str


@tool
async def check_status(service: str) -> str:
    """Look up the current status of a service."""
    return f"{service}: healthy, 3 replicas, 12ms p50 latency"


class OpsAgent(HITLLMAgent):
    name = "ops"
    system = "You are an ops assistant. Use check_status to answer questions about services."
    tools = [check_status]
    consumes = [Consume(Ticket)]


async def main():
    ctx = Context(resources=RuntimeResources(llm=from_env()))
    runtime = Runtime(ctx, groups=[OpsAgent()])
    ctx.create(Ticket(text="is checkout-api healthy?"))
    await runtime.arun()

    from reactifact.tools.use import ToolAnswer
    answer = ctx.latest(ToolAnswer)
    print("answer:", answer.data.text if answer else None)


asyncio.run(main())

No API key configured (from_env() returns None) → the agent honestly says "Could not reach a decision." instead of guessing (§59) — that's not a bug, it's the same honest-fallback contract every generative step in reactifact follows. With a key in .env, the model actually decides to call check_status and answers from its result. To see the full loop run deterministically offline (no key, no guessing), swap resources.llm for a scripted LLMProvider the way tests/test_tools.py's ScriptedLLM does, or reach for reactifact.testing.ScenarioLab if you're writing this as a test.

docs.title: Tools: injection, policies, typed results
docs.text:
A tool parameter annotated with a plain class is a collaborator, resolved from RuntimeResources exactly like a step parameter — it never enters the model's JSON schema. Return a pydantic model and it lands in ToolOutput.data; add retry=/timeout= for transient failures:

from pydantic import BaseModel
from reactifact import RetryPolicy, RuntimeResources, tool
from reactifact.providers import from_env


class Pod(BaseModel):
    name: str


class K8sClient:
    async def get(self, name: str) -> str: ...


@tool(retry=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=3, backoff=0.5), timeout=10)
async def get_pod(name: str, k8s: K8sClient) -> Pod:
    """Read one pod."""
    return Pod(name=await k8s.get(name))


resources = RuntimeResources(llm=from_env())
resources.register(K8sClient, K8sClient())

execute_tool(tool, args, resources=...) injects outside a runtime step (tests, a web job); inside a step the current Context supplies the resources. ToolOutput.error_info (ToolError(retryable=True)) is retried by the same policy; a non-retryable error is returned to the model as data.

Full version: examples/devops — three specialist agents (k8s/GitLab/ Ansible) behind one router, a trace dashboard, a web UI. Run it: .venv/bin/python examples/devops/chat.py.

docs.title: 2. Retrieval over your own docs
docs.text:
Sources are a capability, not a hardcoded RAG pipeline — FileSystemSource here, but CSVSource/WebSource plug into the exact same fan_out_sources call (§8); vector retrieval uses reactifact.knowledge + IndexSource. Provenance is a first-class effect (materialize_doc links the derived Doc back to its SourceRef), not a citation string built by hand:

import asyncio
from pydantic import BaseModel

from reactifact import Context, Runtime, RuntimeResources, create_step_group, step
from reactifact.recipes import fan_out_sources, materialize_doc, find, keyword_score
from reactifact.sources import FileSystemSource, SourceRef


class Question(BaseModel):
    text: str


class Doc(BaseModel):
    text: str


class Answer(BaseModel):
    text: str
    sources: list[str] = []


@step(produces=SourceRef, consumes=Question)
async def search(call):
    question = call.trigger
    await fan_out_sources(call.context, question.data.text, owner_id=question.id, limit=3)


@step(produces=Doc, consumes=SourceRef)
async def resolve(call):
    ref = call.trigger
    await materialize_doc(call.context, ref, lambda ctx, ref, content: Doc(text=content))


@step(produces=Answer, consumes=Doc)
async def answer(call):
    docs = call.inputs
    d = docs[0]
    sources = call.context.related(d.id, "materialized_from")
    return Answer(text=d.data.text.strip(), sources=[s.data.locator for s in sources])


search_group = create_step_group("search", steps=[search])
resolve_group = create_step_group("resolve", steps=[resolve])
answer_group = create_step_group("answer", steps=[answer])


async def main():
    resources = RuntimeResources(
        # the dict key and source_id= must match — that's how a SourceRef
        # finds its way back to the source that produced it (resources.get_source)
        sources={"docs": FileSystemSource("./docs", source_id="docs", scorer=keyword_score)},
    )
    ctx = Context(resources=resources)
    runtime = Runtime(ctx, groups=[search_group, resolve_group, answer_group])
    ctx.create(Question(text="what is your refunds policy?"))
    await runtime.arun()
    a = ctx.latest(Answer)
    print("answer:", a.data.text if a else None)
    print("sources:", a.data.sources if a else None)


asyncio.run(main())

Two easy-to-hit gotchas this snippet already avoids: pass scorer=keyword_score — the plain default scorer has no stop-word filtering, so a query like "what is your refunds policy?" can rank a wrong document up on the word "is" alone; and give FileSystemSource a source_id= that matches the dict key you register it under in resources.sources, since that's the only thing that lets a later materialize_doc resolve a SourceRef back to the source that produced it.

Full version: examples/knowledge — file + CSV sources, evidence extraction, claim verification, deterministic calculation, a keyword-triggered skill. Run it: .venv/bin/python examples/knowledge/chat.py.

docs.title: 3. A session-persisted chat bot
docs.text:
Chat owns sessions, the turn loop, and history reconstruction — your app supplies only the domain models and reply. The same object works as a plain async call (invoke) or, mounted via reactifact.web.create_chat_router, as an SSE endpoint on your own FastAPI app:

import asyncio
from pydantic import BaseModel

from reactifact import Chat, RuntimeResources, SessionStore, create_step_group
from reactifact.checkpoints import FileKVBackend
from reactifact import step


class UserMsg(BaseModel):
    text: str
    session_id: str = ""


class Reply(BaseModel):
    query_id: str
    text: str


@step(produces=Reply, consumes=UserMsg)
async def echo(call):
    msg = call.trigger
    return Reply(query_id=msg.id, text=f"you said: {msg.data.text}")


echo_group = create_step_group("echo", steps=[echo])


def reply(ctx, msg_id):
    latest = ctx.latest(Reply)
    return {"reply": latest.data.text if latest else ""}


async def main():
    store = SessionStore(FileKVBackend("./sessions"))
    assistant = Chat(
        store=store,
        groups=[echo_group],
        seed_type=UserMsg,
        reply=reply,
        resources=RuntimeResources,  # a fresh RuntimeResources per turn
    )
    result = await assistant.invoke("hello there", session_id="demo")
    print(result)                                    # {'reply': 'you said: hello there'}
    print(await assistant.history(session_id="demo"))  # both turns, reconstructed


asyncio.run(main())

Reopen the process and call assistant.invoke(..., session_id="demo") again — the conversation resumes exactly where it left off, because FileKVBackend persisted the whole commit chain, not just the latest reply. To serve this over HTTP instead of calling invoke directly:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from reactifact.web import create_chat_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(create_chat_router(assistant))
# POST /api/chat/stream, GET/DELETE /api/runs/{session_id} — see docs/en/api.md

Full version: examples/devops or examples/knowledge's web.py — real agents behind the same two calls, plus a trace dashboard. resources= there is a callable (lambda: build_resources()) exactly like this snippet, for the same reason: Chat closes a callable-built RuntimeResources after every turn automatically, so a real provider's HTTP client never leaks.

docs.title: Production shape: the FastAPI template
docs.text: The snippets above keep the loop small. For a real web app, copy templates/fastapi_chat: FastAPI Depends auth, scoped sessions, SSE, traces, settings-driven budgets/LLM, tests and Docker. It depends on reactifact[web] itself — the core package still does not pull FastAPI.

docs.title: Where this leaves you
docs.text:
Each snippet above is the smallest reactive version of its pattern — no step of the pipeline calls the next one directly; every step only declares what it consumes/produces, and the runtime derives execution from state changes. That's the same rule the full examples run on, just with more agents, more sources, more error paths. From here:

  • Patterns — more shapes (reflection, map-reduce, supervisor, …).
  • Recipes — the building blocks this page used (fan_out_sources, materialize_doc, find) plus the ones it didn't (StatusMachine, WindowSummarizer, Skill).
  • Examples — all thirteen, with what each one specifically teaches.
  • Port matrix — if you know LangGraph/CrewAI, which example maps to which pattern you already know.
  • Agent skills — the official Agent Skills, installed with python -m reactifact skills install, so a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) can build with reactifact.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text: reactifact.recipes contains reusable building blocks that encode patterns which recur in every demo. Importing reactifact.recipes does not pull in additional dependencies — everything is built on the core.

docs.title: find / find_all — locate typed artifacts in inputs
docs.text:
A step whose agent declares more than one Consume type receives a flat list[Artifact[Any]]; picking out "the one Question" or "all the Evidence" is the same next((a for a in inputs if isinstance(a.data, X)), None) in nearly every step. find/find_all are a typed one-liner for it:

from reactifact.recipes import find, find_all

question = find(inputs, Question)          # Artifact[Question] | None
evidence = find_all(inputs, Evidence)       # list[Artifact[Evidence]]

docs.title: search_sources / fan_out_sources — reactive search
docs.text:
search_sources is the pure part: it fans out and returns ranked, scoped refs without touching the effect slot. Use it when the step wants to create the refs itself (for example, return a list of Emits):

from reactifact import Emit
from reactifact.recipes import search_sources, source_ref_id

query = question.data.text
refs = await search_sources(context, query, owner_id=query_id, limit=5)
return [
    Emit(ref, id=source_ref_id(ref, query_id)) for ref in refs
]

fan_out_sources is the effect-slot wrapper: it does the same search and also writes each ref as a create-or-refresh artifact. Pass effects= to target an explicit slot instead of the current produce's.

from reactifact.recipes import fan_out_sources

refs = await fan_out_sources(
    context,
    query=query,
    owner_id=query_id,           # scope refs to the owning turn
    limit=5,
    query_id=query_id,           # owner key for provenance
    on_start=lambda source: context.announce(
        f"Searching {source}…", kind="status"
    ),
    on_count=lambda source, n: context.announce(
        f"{source}: {n} hits", kind="status"
    ),
)  # each SourceRef is created in the current produce's effects (or effects=)

Pass as_artifacts=True to get the planned Handles instead of the data — the shape materialize_doc accepts in the same produce.

What it does:

  1. Fans out to every configured source in context.resources.sources.
  2. Ranks the combined SourceRefs by score (highest first).
  3. Creates idempotent, owner-scoped refs (effect Create) — id=f"ref:{ref.stable_id()}:{owner_id}".

Idempotency matters: the caller runs a search once per turn (guarded by its own marker) but may re-run on retries; the same ids are re-created, never duplicated. on_start / on_count give you progress announces over SSE.

docs.title: MemoryStore — namespaced long-term memory (§27)
docs.text:
from reactifact.recipes import MemoryStore

memory = MemoryStore(backend, namespace=f"user:{user_id}")
await memory.put(
    "tone",
    {"value": "concise"},
    text="prefers concise answers with citations",
    tags={"kind": "preference"},
    ttl_seconds=90 * 24 * 3600,
)
hits = await memory.search("how should answers be written?", k=3)

Namespaces are mandatory (or set on the store), so a recall cannot read another user/workspace; tags filter, ttl_seconds expires on read/list/search, and search is deterministic keyword ranking (keyword_score, stems/plurals) with a pluggable searcher(record, query) for semantic recall. forget() clears a namespace. Records persist through any KVBackend (file/SQLite/Postgres).

A store is a cross-session index, not a copy of the chat: sessions and checkpoints stay the source of truth. remember_from(artifact, key=…) indexes a curated artifact (a report, a preference) and records its source_session / source_artifact / source_version, so the entry can be rebuilt or erased later:

record = await memory.remember_from(
    report,
    key=f"incident:{report.id}",
    source_session=session_id,          # explicit: request/UserMsg/app state
    text=report.data.text[:800],
    tags={"kind": "report", "system": "k8s"},
)
assert record.source_artifact == report.id
removed = await memory.forget_source(record.source_session)   # GDPR-style

source_session is a required explicit argument — provenance is data, not ambient runtime state. Pass the session from the request/user artifact, or "" when the memory is not tied to one; forget_source("") is rejected so an empty key can never mass-delete sessionless records.

When the write must happen after the artifact commits, use the outbox form from a step; the recipe owns the action payload and the dispatcher:

memory.remember_after_commit(
    effects, report, key=f"incident:{report.id}", source_session=session_id
)
# app: Runtime(..., dispatcher=MemoryStore.dispatch)

remember_after_commit records a PendingAction; MemoryStore.dispatch resolves the registered store from context.resources and calls put after the commit. Unknown action kinds are ignored, so it can be composed with other dispatchers.

docs.title: map_reduce — fan out typed tasks, then reduce (§24)
docs.text:
from reactifact.recipes import map_reduce

result = await map_reduce(
    context,
    items=docs,
    map_fn=lambda payload, index: summarize(payload),
    reduce_fn=lambda rows: merge(rows),
    key="summaries",
    concurrency=8,
    on_error="collect",
)

Each item becomes a stable MapTask (map-task:{key}:{i}); a worker turns it into a MapResult, and a debounced ReduceStep runs once all results for the key exist (map-reduced:{key}). on_error="collect" turns a failing item into a MapResult(error=...) and reduces the rest; "fail_fast" propagates. The child run has its own commit DAG (result.context), reuses the parent tracer/budget, and stamps trace_metadata.parent_run_id.

docs.title: swarm — peer-to-peer handoffs with a guard (§24)
docs.text:
from reactifact.recipes import Handoff, swarm

result = await swarm(
    context,
    groups={"triage": triage, "billing": billing},
    start="triage",
    input=Question(text="refund please"),
    final_type=Answer,
    max_hops=6,
)

An agent creates a Handoff(to=..., reason=..., payload=...); the helper runs that agent from the handoff, records the hop as a Handoff artifact linked to the previous step (handoff_from), and stops at the first non-handoff output (linked derived_from). max_hops is a hard cap; allow_repeat=False also rejects revisiting an agent (SwarmCycle/SwarmLimit). Each hop is a normal subflow, so trace/budget/provenance carry over.

docs.title: materialize_doc — lazy reference resolution
docs.text:
from reactifact.recipes import fan_out_sources, materialize_doc

# `as_artifacts=True` returns planned handles; `materialize_doc` accepts them
refs = await fan_out_sources(
    context, "gpu costs", owner_id="q1", as_artifacts=True
)
doc = await materialize_doc(
    context,
    refs[0],
    doc_type=TypedDoc,
    text_field="content",
    field_map={"path": "locator"},
)

The short form builds the document from doc_type=, filling text_field with the resolved content and matching fields from the ref (locator, source_id, title, query_id, score, metadata). For anything custom, keep the factory form:

async def doc_from_ref(context, ref, content) -> TypedDoc:
    return TypedDoc(query_id=ref.data.query_id, path=..., content=content)

doc = await materialize_doc(
    context, refs[0], doc_from_ref, relation="resolved_from"
)

materialize_doc accepts an Artifact[SourceRef], a plain SourceRef, or a Handle from as_artifacts=True. An already-resolved resolved:{ref_id} doc is reused with refresh=False (the default re-fetches, preserving the old behaviour); a missing source or resolve failure yields None and calls on_error(ref, exc), never a crash.

Because sources return references, not payloads, documents are fetched lazily, only when needed — the rule in the research demo is "resolve a page only after the model ranks it relevant".

The produced document is linked back: TypedDoc ──resolved_from──► SourceRef (§34), so the provenance walk Answer → Claim → Evidence → Doc → SourceRef stays complete.

docs.title: StatusMachine — deterministic lifecycles
docs.text:
Status machines are the pattern for "an artifact that moves through states" (a research turn: researching → answerable → answered). Instead of a manual transition graph, a StatusMachine is a pure function of current state:

from reactifact.recipes import StatusMachine, StatusState


class EvaluateTurn(StatusMachine[ResearchTurn]):
    terminal = frozenset({"answered", "insufficient"})  # where it stops
    query_id_field = "query_id"                  # owner key field (default)
    status_field = "status"                      # status field (default)

    def next_status(self, state: StatusState[ResearchTurn]) -> str | None:
        """Pure function: which status the lifecycle deserves now."""
        if state.any(Answer):
            return "answered"
        return None

    def on_transition(self, context, key, old_status, new_status) -> None:
        context.announce(f"Research status: {old_status} → {new_status}",
                         kind="status", query_id=key)

For a one-method machine, StatusMachine.from_funcs(...) avoids the subclass:

machine = StatusMachine.from_funcs(
    artifact_type=ResearchTurn,
    terminal={"answered", "insufficient"},
    next_status=lambda state: "answered" if state.any(Answer) else None,
)

The constructor form takes the same options: StatusMachine(artifact_type=..., next_status=..., terminal=..., consumes=...).

Mechanics (all inherited from Step):

  • The generic StatusMachine[ResearchTurn] supplies artifact_type; an explicit artifact_type still works.
  • Woken by any event by default; pass consumes= to narrow the wake set. The event maps to a lifecycle via owner_key(artifact) (by default it reads query_id_field of the artifact data, falling back to its id). Override owner_key when a domain uses a different key; StatusState.inputs is filtered with the same hook.
  • Picks the latest matching artifact_type artifact (by updated_at); terminal statuses stop the machine.
  • next_status receives a typed StatusState[StatusT]: the target plus this step's inputs already restricted to key. state.status, state.all(T), state.any(T) and state.latest(T) replace the repeated list_artifacts(T) + query_id == key filtering.
  • next_status decides the new status; None or unchanged ⇒ nothing happens.
  • Right before applying the change, on_transition(context, key, old_status, new_status) is called — your hook for progress announces.
  • The transition is a return-style Edit(target, **{status_field: new}), which compiles to the same update effect; the machine declares produces=() because it updates its target rather than creating a new artifact.

Put your verify logic into another step that reacts on status changes — the machine and the verifier are separate, deterministic, and unit-testable. The knowledge demo's EvaluateTurn is the canonical instance of this recipe.

docs.title: TurnContextStep — one conversation context per turn
docs.text:
Transcript renders a window but still takes Context; TurnContextStep turns the common chat shape into one artifact: current query, previous query, bounded history, rolling digest and a follow-up flag. Downstream steps consume TurnContext and never reconstruct the conversation themselves.

from reactifact.recipes.conversation import TurnFacts, TurnContextStep

def build_dialogue(facts: TurnFacts) -> DialogueContext:
    return DialogueContext(
        query_id=facts.trigger.id,
        history="\n".join(m.text for m in facts.history),
        prior_question=facts.previous_query or "",
        prior_answer=(
            facts.previous_answer.data.text
            if facts.previous_answer is not None
            else ""
        ),
    )

turn_context = TurnContextStep(
    UserQuery,
    assistant_type=Answer,
    digest_type=Digest,         # optional; reads digest_id="digest"
    artifact_type=DialogueContext,  # custom build target
    window=12,
    consume=OnCreate(UserQuery),    # or a plain Consume
    ensure=True,                    # idempotent per turn
    follow_up=my_follow_up,         # optional; deterministic default
    build=build_dialogue,           # turns TurnFacts into your artifact
)

# groups=[turn_context, *answer_steps]

The step emits TurnContext (or artifact_type=) with id turn:{trigger.id}; history is bounded to the current trigger (later turns are not included) and keeps the turn/session_id fields. TurnFacts includes the trigger, current/previous query, previous artifact/answer, history, digest and follow-up flag — so a domain context can carry prior_domain/routing_text without reading Context. consume=OnCreate makes it one artifact per turn; ensure=True makes a re-run a no-op. Combine with Annotated[..., Unscoped()] when another step also needs full history.

docs.title: WindowSummarizer — periodic conversation checkpoints (§27, §37)
docs.text:
Long-running chat memory is just state: message artifacts accumulate, and a summarizer condenses the recent window every N messages into a checkpoint artifact. The recipe owns the window size, cadence, and idempotency; the domain owns how to summarize and what the summary artifact looks like:

from reactifact.recipes import WindowSummarizer, llm_summarizer


class Summary(BaseModel):
    round: int
    text: str


def build_summary(round_no: int, text: str) -> Summary:
    return Summary(round=round_no, text=text)


class Flow(StepGroup):
    name = "chat"
    consumes = [Consume(Msg)]
    steps = [
        WindowSummarizer(
            Msg, Summary,
            summarize=llm_summarizer("Condense the recent conversation into a short memory note."),
            build=build_summary,
            window=8,   # messages fed into one summary
            every=4,    # produce a new checkpoint every N messages
        ),
    ]
  • summarize(context, history) -> str | None — your callback (or llm_summarizer(system=...), a thin wrapper over llm_reply); None triggers the recipe's fallback (default: a truncated-history string, never a crash).
  • build(round_no, text) -> Summary — you own the summary artifact's shape; the recipe never guesses field names.
  • The summary id is derived from the message count (summary:{round} by default), so re-running the same generation never duplicates a summary. Batched creation is handled: the latest completed round is produced even when several messages arrive in one generation.
  • render/order_key/id_of are all overridable if the defaults (role/text rendering, created_at ordering) don't fit your artifact.
  • message_type also accepts a sequence of types (e.g. [UserQuery, Answer]), so one checkpoint covers a heterogeneous thread.

Do not pair it with WindowPruner. The checkpoint cadence is based on the message count, and pruning stops that count from growing, so the next checkpoint never arrives. Use RollingDigestSummarizer when the raw window must be bounded (and summarized), or WindowPruner alone when you only need a bounded raw transcript:

from reactifact.recipes import WindowPruner

steps = [WindowPruner(Msg, keep=8)]

WindowPruner is also standalone-useful and accepts the same single type or sequence of types.

See tests/test_recipes_memory.py for the runnable cases.

docs.title: RollingDigestSummarizer — one growing memory instead of per-round checkpoints (§27, §37)
docs.text:
WindowSummarizer keeps every round's snapshot around; some apps instead want a single memory note that keeps accumulating, with only a small raw tail kept verbatim. RollingDigestSummarizer is that other shape: once the conversation passes trigger messages, it folds everything older than window into one digest artifact — each fold rewrites the digest from the previous digest text plus the newly stale messages — and deletes the folded messages itself:

from reactifact.recipes import RollingDigestSummarizer, llm_digest_summarizer


class Digest(BaseModel):
    text: str


def build_digest(text: str) -> Digest:
    return Digest(text=text)


class Flow(StepGroup):
    name = "chat"
    consumes = [Consume(Msg)]
    steps = [
        RollingDigestSummarizer(
            Msg, Digest,
            summarize=llm_digest_summarizer("Fold the new messages into the running memory note."),
            build=build_digest,
            window=8,    # messages kept raw
            trigger=12,  # fold once the conversation passes this length
        ),
    ]
  • message_type takes a single type or a sequence of types — e.g. [Question, FinalResponse] when a conversation is two artifact types interleaved rather than one Msg model. They're merged and ordered by order_key before the window/trigger math runs.
  • summarize(context, previous_digest_text, stale_artifacts) -> str | None gets the stale artifacts as a raw list, not a pre-rendered string — the recipe never flattens messages into text for you. That matters when you already have a role/content prompt builder, or the message types don't reduce to one role/text shape: write your own rendering inside summarize and there's no round-trip through this recipe's string format to worry about. llm_digest_summarizer(system=...) is the opt-in default for callers who do want a plain text-in/text-out prompt — it renders with role: text lines (override via its own render=) and labels the previous digest and the new history as two sections of one user turn. None from either path triggers fallback, which defaults to appending a truncated-history line to the previous digest rather than dropping it.
  • build(text) -> Digest — you own the digest artifact's shape; digest_text is the matching reader (default: artifact.data.text) if your shape doesn't use a text field.
  • The digest lives at one stable id (digest by default, via digest_id) — each fold refreshes it in place rather than creating a new artifact.
  • Don't pair this with WindowPruner: pruning deletes without folding first, which loses the content this recipe means to condense. It manages its own raw window and needs nothing else.

docs.title: llm_digest_summarizer and ChatMemory.from_transcript
docs.text:
llm_digest_summarizer covers the whole "fold stale turns into a digest" callback, including the fallback policy:

from reactifact.recipes.conversation import MessageSpec, Transcript
from reactifact.recipes.memory import llm_digest_summarizer

transcript = Transcript([
    MessageSpec(UserQuery, "user"),
    MessageSpec(Answer, "assistant"),
])

summarize = llm_digest_summarizer(
    SUMMARY_SYSTEM,
    user=SUMMARY_USER,             # PromptTemplate with {previous}/{history}
    render=transcript.render,      # typed role lines
    schema=AnswerBody,             # structured call; omit for plain text
    max_fallback_chars=4000,
    attempts=1,
    temperature=0.2,
    max_tokens=800,
)
memory = ChatMemory.from_transcript(
    transcript,
    keep=settings.chat_memory_keep,
    summarize=summarize,
    summary_type=ConversationDigest,
    compact_commits=settings.chat_memory_commits,
)

The callback returns the previous digest when there is no new history, skips the LLM when context.resources.llm is None, and falls back to previous + "\n" + history (truncated) when the provider raises, returns None, or returns blank text. fallback= overrides that policy.

docs.title: Route — one case group per artifact value
docs.text:
Route is for the common "the turn carries a branch key; only one downstream group should run" shape. It stays a builder over ordinary StepGroups — no nested groups in the runtime. Each case group keeps its own steps and later triggers; only matches of the route's on event are narrowed by key(value) == case.

from reactifact.recipes import Route

route = Route(
    on=ResearchTurn,
    key=lambda turn: turn.domain,
    cases={
        "meta": kb_react_group,
        "rag": rag_group,
    },
    default="rag",       # values outside the map use the rag group
)

Runtime(ctx, groups=[*route.groups(), planner, ...])

Generated groups carry a route_case marker. validate_contracts uses it to suppress the ambiguous_producer warning when the same artifact is produced by distinct cases of one route; producers outside the route still warn.

docs.title: ScopedCleanup — drop a turn's scratch by scope
docs.text:
EphemeralCleanup removes artifacts whose ids are derived from a terminal artifact's key. The chat variant has arbitrary ids but a shared scope (query_id): ScopedCleanup reacts to OnCreate(Answer) and drops every scratch artifact in that scope, leaving other turns untouched. In the example, Answer is the app's terminal artifact type.

from reactifact import OnCreate
from reactifact.recipes.cleanup import ScopedCleanup

cleanup = ScopedCleanup(
    Answer,
    scratch_types=(DialogueContext, TurnIntent, ResearchTurn, Evidence),
    scope="query_id",          # or a Scope(...)
    consume=OnCreate(Answer),  # default
)

# groups=[create_step_group("cleanup", steps=[cleanup])]

It declares produces=() and the real deletes=(...), so contracts no longer claim the cleanup creates an Answer. The related_all(type) lookup is scoped by the terminal's key; a scratch type produced outside that scope is left alone. scope is required (pass None explicitly for a deliberate global cleanup).

docs.title: run_tool_loop — a bounded native tool-calling loop (§46, §47)
docs.text:
reactifact.tools.native deliberately ships one-turn helpers, not a loop. When you do want the loop — bounded rounds, parallel calls, a forced final answer — run_tool_loop is the opt-in recipe; it is not a reactive StepGroup:

from reactifact.recipes import parse_tool_calls_with_textual, run_tool_loop

result = await run_tool_loop(
    call.context,
    system="You are a research assistant.",
    user=question,
    tools=[search_knowledge, read_source],
    mandatory="read_source",
    max_rounds=6,
    max_observation_chars=4_000,   # cap what goes back into the prompt
    redact_tool_outputs=True,      # apply resources.redactor to tool output
    parse_calls=parse_tool_calls_with_textual,  # tolerate DSML/XML providers
    on_event=lambda name, payload: ...,         # round/tool/final for SSE
)
call.effects.create(Answer(text=result.text))
  • The turn's Budget is honoured between rounds: max_tool_calls caps executions (extra calls come back as tool errors), max_seconds and token/cost limits stop new rounds; the loop then forces an answer.
  • fallback(ctx, messages, text) runs when no calls were parsed and the text looks like tool-call markup (looks_like_tool_markup); return a string to end the turn (e.g. delegate to a legacy ToolUse loop), or None to accept the text as the answer.
  • on_event receives round_start, tool_call, tool_result, final; the same progress is published through Context.announce(kind="agent"), so a Chat(status_kinds=("status", "agent")) streams it without a custom loop.
  • ToolLoopResult.stop_reason is completed, max_rounds, budget, provider_error or fallback; error carries the provider failure detail. Tool failures are also typed: ToolOutput.failed(ToolError(code=, message=, retryable=)) surfaces as ToolObservation.error_info, and retry_tool_errors=True retries only the retryable=True ones (tool_retry_attempts/tool_retry_delay control the backoff; retries count as tool executions for Budget.max_tool_calls).

docs.title: keyword_score / stem_words — deterministic text scoring (§67)
docs.text:
Where embeddings are optional, keyword coverage is the neutral fallback (the English knowledge chat and the Russian repair catalog use it):

from reactifact.recipes import EN_STOPWORDS, keyword_score, stem_words

keyword_score("How to set up authentication", "authentication")          # 1.0
keyword_score("Установка аутентификации", "аутентификацию", use_stems=True)  # 1.0
stem_words("Ремонт комнаты и kitchen")  # {"ремонт", "комнат", "kitchen"}
  • English stop words are removed from both sides by default (EN_STOPWORDS).
  • use_stems=True applies a small Russian inflectional stemmer, so «аутентификацию» matches «аутентификация» without a model.

docs.title: Skills — keyword-triggered instruction snippets (§67)
docs.text:
A skill is the same shape popularized by Claude's Skills: a markdown file with a name/description frontmatter and a body of procedural instructions. It is not a Source — a Source is retrieved to answer a question with facts; a skill is loaded to change how an LLM call for the current turn is made (a rule to follow, a format to use) once its description matches the situation:

from reactifact.recipes import load_skills, match_skills

# --- once, at startup ---
skills = load_skills("skills/")   # every *.md file, parsed by frontmatter

# --- per turn, only where it applies ---
situation = "reporting an answer backed by a number computed from structured storage"
for skill in match_skills(skills, situation):
    prompt += f"\n\nInstruction ({skill.name}): {skill.body}"

A skill file:

---
name: cost-reporting
description: How to report a number computed from structured storage. Use when the answer is backed by a deterministic calculation.
---
State the exact computed value explicitly, and say plainly it was computed,
not estimated — name the source and column it came from.
  • situation is a short, code-written description of what is currently happening, not necessarily the user's raw question — the caller characterizes the moment, the same way the skill's own description characterizes when to use it. This keeps triggering reactive (§8): a skill fires because of what state exists (e.g. a Calculation artifact), not because the code parses the user's phrasing.
  • Matching is keyword_score (deterministic, no embeddings) over name + description; only matches at or above threshold (default 0.34) are returned, capped at limit (default 1) — a skill should be a precise trigger, not a fallback that fires on every turn.
  • This is deliberately not a new core primitive (§61): a matched skill's body is just a string you prepend to a structured_llm/llm_reply prompt. The knowledge demo's cost-reporting skill (examples/knowledge/skills/) is the canonical instance — see its README.
  • Scope: this covers the instructions half of Claude's Skills format — frontmatter + procedural markdown. It does not cover the other half — bundled executable scripts a skill can ship and have the model run. That's a deliberate line, not a gap to close: executing a skill's own code is a sandboxing and permissions problem, and reactifact's determinism story (§67) is about not handing the runtime code to execute unreviewed. If you need that, wire the script as a Tool yourself (§46) — reachable from a matched skill's body (name it in the instructions) or independent of it.

docs.title: PlanExecute — sequential plan → execute → finish (§24, §42, §69)
docs.text:
Plan-and-Execute (LangChain/AutoGPT-style): a plan is drafted once, its steps run one at a time — each gated on its predecessor's result — and a final answer is synthesized once every step has one. Ported from The PlanExecute recipe's Planner/Executor/Finisher (141 + 14 lines), generalized: the recipe owns ordering, gating, idempotent re-entry, and completion detection; you only implement the three decisions that need judgement.

from reactifact.recipes import PlanExecute


class Flow(PlanExecute[Goal, PlanStep, StepResult, FinalAnswer]):
    goal_type = Goal
    step_type = PlanStep
    result_type = StepResult
    final_type = FinalAnswer

    async def plan(self, context, goal) -> list[PlanStep]:
        ...  # ordered steps — index/goal are stamped by the recipe

    async def execute_step(self, context, step, history) -> StepResult:
        ...  # history: every prior step's result, in order

    async def finish(self, context, goal, results) -> FinalAnswer:
        ...  # combine every step's result, in order


class FlowAgent(StepGroup):
    consumes = [Consume(Goal), Consume(PlanStep), Consume(StepResult)]
    steps = Flow().produces()

The same flow without a subclass — and with the group/pipeline wiring inferred:

from reactifact.recipes import PlanExecute

flow = PlanExecute.from_funcs(
    goal_type=Goal,
    step_type=PlanStep,
    result_type=StepResult,
    final_type=FinalAnswer,
    plan=plan,                    # sync or async
    execute_step=execute_step,
    finish=finish,
)
pipeline = flow.pipeline(seed_type=Goal)   # or flow.group() in a Runtime
result = pipeline.run(Goal(text="ship it"))
  • step_type/result_type need goal_field/index_field (defaults: "goal"/"index") with defaults on the fields (e.g. index: int = 0) — the recipe stamps the real values on every create, your hooks don't need to fill them in.
  • Supports several goals concurrently in one Context — steps/results are scoped by goal_field, not by "whatever's in the Context right now".
  • Provenance: the final artifact is linked supported_by → every step result (§34).

See tests/test_recipe_plan_execute.py for the runnable cases.

docs.title: Router / ApprovalGate — classify, then ask before finalizing (§60, §67)
docs.text:
Two independent pieces: a router and an approval gate. The pattern mirrors RouteTask/Supervisor produces:

  • Router — classify a request into one of a fixed set of routes, idempotently, with a deterministic fallback when the classifying call is unavailable or returns something outside routes (§67).
  • ApprovalGate — ask a human to sign off on a report before finalizing it (§60). Tracks a thread's whole history of approval questions, not just the unanswered ones, so a rejection doesn't spawn a duplicate question chain — the exact bookkeeping bug this recipe exists to not let you write again. Uses kind="approve" — the same vocabulary the destructive-tool gate (reactifact.tools.use) and Verify (verify.py) already use, so one control-plane UI built for "approve" requests handles all three.
from reactifact.recipes import ApprovalGate, Router


class MyRouter(Router[Request, Task]):
    request_type = Request
    task_type = Task
    routes = ("budget", "timeline", "quality")

    async def classify(self, context, request) -> str | None:
        ...  # structured LLM decision, or None to fall back

    def fallback_route(self, context, request) -> str:
        ...  # deterministic keyword match, etc.


class MyGate(ApprovalGate[SpecialistReport, FinalReply]):
    report_type = SpecialistReport
    final_type = FinalReply

    def approval_question(self, context, report) -> str: ...
    async def on_approve(self, context, report) -> FinalReply: ...
    async def on_reject(self, context, report, answer) -> FinalReply: ...


class Flow(StepGroup):
    consumes = [Consume(Request), Consume(Task), Consume(SpecialistReport),
                Consume(PendingQuestion)]
    steps = [MyRouter().produce(), Specialist(), MyGate().produce(),
             Step(PendingQuestion)]  # Router/ApprovalGate call human.ask at runtime

Specialist — actually doing the routed work — stays fully your own Step; there's nothing generic about "what a route does".

See tests/test_recipe_supervisor.py for the runnable cases.

docs.title: ReflectionLoop — generate → critique → regenerate (§24, §42, §69)
docs.text:
LangGraph's "Reflection" pattern. The recipe mirrors the hand-rolled hand-rolled DraftIt/Critic/Rewrite/Finalize produces. Unlike PlanExecute (immutable, indexed steps), the working state is one mutable draft artifact per topic, updated in place each round — matching the ported example's own effects.update(draft, ...) model.

from reactifact.recipes import ReflectionLoop


class MyLoop(ReflectionLoop[Topic, Draft, Review, Final]):
    topic_type = Topic
    draft_type = Draft
    review_type = Review
    final_type = Final
    accept_at = 0.8
    max_rounds = 2

    async def draft(self, context, topic) -> Draft: ...
    async def critique(self, context, draft) -> tuple[float, str]: ...  # (score, feedback)
    async def rewrite(self, context, draft, feedback) -> Draft: ...
    async def finish(self, context, draft) -> Final: ...


class Flow(StepGroup):
    consumes = [Consume(Topic), Consume(Draft), Consume(Review)]
    steps = MyLoop().produces()

Function-first is the same shape:

loop = ReflectionLoop.from_funcs(
    topic_type=Topic,
    draft_type=Draft,
    review_type=Review,
    final_type=Final,
    draft=draft,
    critique=critique,            # (score, feedback), sync or async
    rewrite=rewrite,
    finish=finish,
    accept_at=0.85,
)
pipeline = loop.pipeline(seed_type=Topic)
  • draft_type needs topic_field/round_field/status_field (defaults: "topic"/"round"/"status"); review_type needs topic_field too — a Review is only ever reached by reacting to its own creation, so the recipe must read the topic straight off it. Give these fields defaults; the recipe stamps the real values on every create/update.
  • Round-capping (max_rounds) and the accept threshold (accept_at) are the recipe's — not scattered if round + 1 > MAX_ROUNDS checks across three produces.
  • Supports several topics concurrently in one Context.

See tests/test_recipe_reflection.py for the runnable cases.

docs.title: changed_fields / earliest_stage / downstream_fields — change → rebuild
docs.text:
Long multi-stage flows occasionally have to go back: the user edits a fact, the pipeline rebuilds from the earliest affected stage and clears everything downstream. The helpers are generic; the workflow is your field_stages map and stage order (the repair approval is the canonical usage):

from reactifact.recipes import changed_fields, downstream_fields, earliest_stage

field_stages = {"room": "collect", "style": "design_choice",
                "area": "plan", "budget": "estimate"}
order = ("collect", "design_choice", "plan", "estimate")

changed = changed_fields(old_info, new_info)          # {"style", "budget"}
target = earliest_stage(changed, field_stages=field_stages, order=order)
reset = downstream_fields(target, field_stages=field_stages, order=order)

changed_fields ignores fields the new state left None (the model didn't know); earliest_stage returns None when nothing changed; downstream_fields is target-inclusive (everything at that stage or later is reset, upstream kept).

docs.title: Release management
docs.text: How a reactifact version is cut, built, verified, and published.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
• SemVer; pre-releases carry an rc mark (e.g. 0.20.0rc1), dropped for the stable cut (0.20.0).
  • The version lives in one place: pyproject.toml → [project] version. reactifact.__version__ reads the installed distribution metadata; tests/test_version.py guards the match.

docs.title: Changelog rule
docs.text:
Every user-visible change lands in CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog). Cut the entry when the version is bumped:

  1. move unreleased items under a new ## [X.Y.Z] — <date> heading;
  2. group them as Added / Changed / Removed (deprecations too);
  3. put every breaking change under a ### Breaking heading, even in rcs.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
0.25.0 has a migration guide; 0.24.0 has its own; 0.23.0 has its own; 0.20.0 has its own. CHANGELOG.md remains the source of truth for what changed between versions, and breaking entries are marked per the rule above. A few changes worth knowing if you're crossing them (see also migrating.md for porting from other frameworks):

  • 0.25.0 — mostly additive ergonomics: scope= on Step/@step, cross-turn Unscoped(), the TurnContext recipe, side-effect-only steps, typed CurrentRequest, Step.progress, [tool.reactifact] config, and skills install --target opencode|all|auto. Two planned removals break compatibility: EmbeddingSource (use the knowledge layer + IndexSource) and the 0.20 tool-module shims (use reactifact.tools.*). See the 0.25 migration guide.
  • 0.24.0 — CLI/daemon/MCP/HTTP adapter work, check, new agent, demo --web, pipeline tools and HITL/approval recipes. The LLM helpers (structured_llm, json_schema_llm, llm_reply, chat_complete*, StructuredLLM.call) now take an LLMProvider (or None), not a Context. Agent, create_agent, validate_agents, agents= and the reactifact.agents module are removed; use StepGroup, create_step_group, validate_contracts(groups=...) and groups=.
  • 0.23.0 — the typed Chat facade (answer/traces/lifespan/test_client), Inject/Depends tool DI, typed tool results and structured tool errors, function-first PlanExecute/ReflectionLoop, tail trace sampling and retention. Produce/@produce/ProduceCall, also_creates=/reacts_to= and Effects.ask/resume/act are removed (the last has no prior deprecation release; use Human/Outbox); the remaining deprecated bridges are documented in the 0.23 migration guide.
  • 0.22.0 — CLI scaffolding (new app|daemon, doctor) and bundled FastAPI/daemon templates (FastAPI remains an optional core extra); provenance-aware MemoryStore with post-commit indexing; per-request chat resources; typed run events, checkpoints/forks, retries/timeouts, tool record/replay, swarm/map_reduce, optimistic concurrency/merge policies, typed HITL answers and trace scopes. Produce/ProduceCall/@produce leave the top-level __all__ and are removed in 0.23.0.
  • 0.21.0 — the optional, code-first reactifact.knowledge layer: Connector → RawDocument → Document → Chunk → Index, incremental DocStore state, FilesystemConnector, hybrid BM25 + RRF retrieval, MemoryIndex / SqliteIndex / QdrantIndex / ChromaIndex / PgVectorIndex, a domain rerank= hook plus llm_reranker, and an optional knowledge status router. IndexSource / IngestStep are the explicit bridges into Source / Step; core has no new runtime dependency.
  • 0.20.0 — the new core line. Step/@step replace the Produce authoring surface; class steps take effects: Effects (self.effects is gone); Artifact is a frozen handle over a content-addressed version store; sessions use the v2 blobs/data_ref format; and the legacy example set was removed. Produce, ProduceCall, @produce, StepGroup.produces, Artifact.at/history/ diff and the top-level tool-module shims remain importable for the 0.21 compatibility window; Produce/ProduceCall/@produce are no longer part of the top-level __all__; Produce/ProduceCall/@produce are removed in 0.23.0, while the other bridges are kept through 0.24.0.
  • 0.14.0 — behavior-visible (non-breaking) changes to know about:
  • Budget.max_seconds is now a hard turn deadline: the runtime cancels the generation in flight when it passes (a hung LLM call is actually stopped) and ends the turn with RunOutcome.BUDGET_TIME_EXCEEDED; the cancelled generation's trigger batch is left queued for a resume. Before, the check only ran between generations, so a run could overshoot it.
  • A new RunOutcome.STOPPED is reported when Runtime.request_stop() / ashutdown() ends a run at a generation boundary.
  • Logging is silent by default — nothing is emitted under reactifact.* until configure_logging() is called.
  • 0.11.0 — behavior-visible (non-breaking) changes to know about:
  • RunTrace.duration_ms is now milliseconds (it carried raw time.monotonic() seconds before, so the dashboard showed 0 ms and the Langfuse run span ended ~1000× too early). RunStats.duration stays seconds.
  • RunTrace.started_at is now the turn start (previously the end), and AgentSpan.started_at is persisted (SQLite/Postgres auto-migrate) to power the dashboard timeline.
  • The TraceReader protocol grew a sessions() read; the dashboard's create_trace_router now expects a TraceStoreProtocol (read + the tag annotation methods). The built-in TraceStore/PostgresStore satisfy it; a custom reader implementing only query/get needs sessions() and the annotation methods for the new pages to work.
  • 0.10.0 — behavior-visible (non-breaking) changes to know about:
  • PromptTemplate.render now substitutes only identifier-shaped {field} placeholders and leaves other braces verbatim, so a literal JSON example in a prompt needs no {{/}} escaping. A placeholder inside a JSON object still needs the object's outer braces doubled ({{"answer": "{answer}"}}). Templates that relied on str.format treating a stray {...} as an error/format-spec now pass it through.
  • reactifact.chat.ChatEvent.kind is a closed Literal["session","status","message"]; constructing one with an arbitrary kind now fails validation.
  • Provider/WebSource/OTLP/Langfuse HTTP clients are created lazily per event loop (no more RuntimeError: Event loop is closed across loops); an injected client= is still used as-is.
  • Runtime.arun/astream gained a keyword-only request=; Runtime.run/ run_once likewise. Existing positional calls are unaffected.
  • 0.7.0 — Context.merge_from now preserves the id of an artifact that exists in other but not in target (it previously minted a fresh one). If you relied on the old id-regenerating behavior — unlikely, since it silently detached the merged artifact from any relation pointing at its original id — pass the artifact through create(data, id=new_id()) yourself before merging to keep the old effect.
  • 0.2.0 — reactifact/__init__.py re-exports only the core surface (~40 names, down from ~150); eval, tracing, checkpoint/branch backends, the chat/web layer, the adaptive scheduler, replay, structured-LLM helpers, viz, and prompt templates moved to their own submodule imports. Nothing renamed — see the ### Breaking entry in CHANGELOG.md for the full before/after import list.
  • 0.4.0-rc1 — LLMRequest.temperature changed from a hard-coded 0.7 to float | None; None now means "omit → provider default" instead of "use 0.7". Same call shape, different generation behavior, no error raised — pass temperature=0.7 explicitly (per-call or on the provider) if your code relied on the old implicit default.
  • 0.1.0-rc1 — Produce no longer returns a Patch; it writes effects.create/update/link/ask/resume and returns None (see effects). InterruptPatch, Patch.merge_existing_patch and Patch.to_dict were removed.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
What must be true before cutting a release — and, specifically, the bar for leaving pre-1.0 and shipping 1.0.0:

  • [ ] uv run python -m pytest -q is green, coverage ≥ the fail_under floor (and reactifact/quota.py, metrics.py, eval/ not the tail).
  • [ ] uv run python -m mypy and uv run python -m ruff check / ruff format --check are clean.
  • [ ] uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict is clean (CI enforces it).
  • [ ] The public surface is unchanged except as the freeze test (tests/test_public_api.py) and docs/en/api.md §Stability record; any rename/removal has a ### Breaking changelog entry and a deprecation window behind it.
  • [ ] The wheel smoke job passes in a clean venv (uv build, import, CLI).
  • [ ] CHANGELOG.md moves [Unreleased] under ## [X.Y.Z] — <date>.
  • [ ] tests/test_version.py passes (distribution metadata matches reactifact.__version__).

1.0 criteria (all of the above, plus):

  • [ ] Two consecutive minor releases with no ### Breaking entry.
  • [ ] Every documented submodule __all__ is pinned by the freeze test and reflected in docs/en/api.md.
  • [ ] The safety/eval/observability surfaces (guardrails, authz, quota, eval, online eval, metrics, tracing) each have usage docs and tests.
  • [ ] No rc/Unreleased-only guarantees leak into the contract.

docs.title: The release loop
docs.text:
# 1) sanity
.venv/bin/python -m pytest
.venv/bin/python -m mypy
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check
.venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check
.venv/bin/lint-imports
uv lock --check

# 2) version + changelog (see above)

# 3) build artifacts (clean stale build/ + dist/ first; setuptools reuses build/lib)
rm -rf build dist *.egg-info
uv build                     # dist/reactifact-0.25.0-py3-none-any.whl + sdist

# 4) verify the wheel in a scratch venv (not the workspace, so no PYTHONPATH)
uv venv /tmp/reactifact-rc
uv pip install --python /tmp/reactifact-rc/bin/python --quiet dist/reactifact-0.25.0-py3-none-any.whl
/tmp/reactifact-rc/bin/python -c "import reactifact; print(reactifact.__version__)"
/tmp/reactifact-rc/bin/python -m reactifact graph examples.knowledge.step_groups 2>/dev/null \
    || /tmp/reactifact-rc/bin/reactifact --help >/dev/null   # console script present
# confirm the wheel contains reactifact + tracing templates and NOT examples/tests:
unzip -l dist/reactifact-0.25.0-py3-none-any.whl | grep -E "examples/|tests/|tracing/templates"

# 5) tag
git tag v0.25.0
git push origin v0.25.0

# 6) publish (PyPI token in env); publish only the new files, not an old dist/
uv publish --publish-url https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/ dist/reactifact-0.25.0*

docs.title: What ships
docs.text: The wheel packages only the reactifact package (setuptools packages.find excludes examples/tests) plus the trace dashboard assets (reactifact/tracing/templates/*.html and *.css). The sdist also carries the test suite for downstream packagers; examples and docs stay in the repository and are the documentation-by-example.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: A broken rc is fixed in the next rc/release — never rewrite history of a tagged version. Keep patch releases strictly backwards-compatible (§61: the framework is stable at the stated surface).

docs.title: Replay (§55)
docs.text: Replay answers the constitutive question — "why did the agent produce this answer?" — concretely. Because commits are deterministic (§14), context state is recoverable without running agents, and because every LLM call can be recorded, a run can be reproduced exactly.

docs.title: Provider-level record & replay
docs.text:
ReplayLLM is a recording studio for the model calls. Two passes:

from reactifact.replay import ReplayLLM

# pass 1 — record a real run
resources = RuntimeResources(
    llm=ReplayLLM("calls.jsonl", mode="record", inner=real_llm)
)
runtime.run()                          # appends every call to calls.jsonl

# pass 2 — reproduce the run without any network
resources = RuntimeResources(llm=ReplayLLM("calls.jsonl", mode="replay"))
runtime.run()                          # same artifacts, same answers
  • mode="record" wraps a real provider and appends each (request → response) pair (model, temperature, response_format, messages → text, usage) as one JSONL line.
  • mode="replay" answers exactly the recorded calls. A call that does not match the recording raises ReplayMiss — it must not be answered with a wrong result (§59). At the structured_llm layer the miss degrades to an honest None (the normal fallback path).

Because the deterministic paths (guards, calculations, routing) are unchanged, a replayed run produces identical artifacts — and you can walk the reproduced state (or render it with context_to_mermaid) to explain the answer.

docs.title: Tool-level record & replay
docs.text:
The same idea covers framework tool calls (execute_tool, used by ToolUse/run_tool_loop):

from reactifact.replay import RecordingToolRecorder, ReplayToolRecorder

record = RuntimeResources(tool_recorder=RecordingToolRecorder("tools.jsonl"))
# ... run once; every execute_tool call appends name/args/output (or exception)

replay = RuntimeResources(tool_recorder=ReplayToolRecorder("tools.jsonl"))
# ... run again; calls match by (tool, exact args), FIFO for repeats

A call with no matching record raises ReplayMiss — never a silently wrong tool result. A recorded exception is re-raised as RuntimeError with the original message. Both execute_tool(...) and a direct tool.execute(...) inside a Runtime turn are instrumented (the wrapper is on Tool itself); use begin_tool_runs/end_tool_runs to open the same scope around direct calls outside a Runtime.

docs.title: One-call replay: Runtime.replay_run
docs.text:
Runtime.replay_run() temporarily installs the replay wrappers, runs the normal turn, and restores the resources:

await runtime.replay_run(
    llm_recording="calls.jsonl",
    tool_recording="tools.jsonl",
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",   # part of the LLM recording key
)

save=False (default) detaches the session so a replay never overwrites the recorded session; pass save=True if you intentionally want to persist the reproduced artifacts.

docs.title: Verify a run is reproducible
docs.text:
Recording pins the model, but a run is only truly reproducible if nothing else is nondeterministic either — the usual culprits are auto-generated artifact ids (uuid4), wall-clock time, and randomness. verify_run runs your pipeline several times under a recorded model and strict, deterministic ids, then compares the resulting context_hash:

from reactifact import Context, Runtime
from reactifact.replay import verify_run


async def build(resources):
    context = Context(resources=resources)
    context.create(Question(...))
    await Runtime(context, groups=GROUPS).arun()
    return context


report = await verify_run(build, recording="calls.jsonl")   # runs twice
assert report.ok, report.hashes

A difference is real nondeterminism in your code (an unstable id, time.time(), uuid4() in artifact data, order), not model variance — report.hashes shows the diverging fingerprints. When you build resources yourself, passing RuntimeResources(id_factory=counter_ids()) makes artifacts created without an explicit id get stable Model:0000-style ids instead of uuid4 — often the whole fix. This is what the fintech_audit example does, and why re-running it prints the same context sha256.

docs.title: Deterministic state replay
docs.text:
A session checkpoint carries the full commit chain. Reconstruct the state at a specific commit without agent execution:

from reactifact.replay import replay_context, replay_summary
from reactifact.checkpoints import SQLiteKVBackend
from reactifact.session import SessionStore

store = SessionStore(SQLiteKVBackend("sessions.sqlite3"))
context = await replay_context(store, session_id, version=7)   # state at commit 7
print(replay_summary(context))                                  # counts, by type

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
python -m reactifact replay sessions.sqlite3 --session demo --diagram

Prints the replayed state summary (version · artifacts · relations · pending questions, breakdown by artifact type; a dispatched / pending / failed line when the run used the outbox, §42) and, with --diagram, the provenance graph as Mermaid. --version replays to a specific commit.

Replay is state reconstruction, not re-execution: it never runs the runtime, so a recorded PendingAction (an email, a webhook) is read back as state and never re-sent. That is the point — you can explain why the agent acted without acting again.

docs.title: Trust & safety
docs.text: Three opt-in, library-level layers for running reactifact with untrusted input and multiple principals. They act on typed artifacts and resource access, so they are deterministic and testable — unlike middleware wrapped around model messages. Everything is configured on RuntimeResources and is off by default.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
A guardrail validates or rewrites an artifact's data before the runtime commits it. Every Create/Update an agent produces is checked:

from reactifact import RuntimeResources
from reactifact.guardrails import GuardrailPolicy, InjectionGuardrail, PIIGuardrail
from reactifact.redaction import RegexRedactor

resources = RuntimeResources(
    guardrails=GuardrailPolicy(
        [PIIGuardrail(redactor=RegexRedactor()), InjectionGuardrail()],
        on_violation="block",          # or "flag"
    ),
)

A guardrail is any object with name and check(data, context) -> GuardrailDecision. The decision is allow, redact (with the replacement data), violation (defer to the policy's on_violation), or block/flag (override the policy for that guardrail). Built-ins:

Guardrail Checks PIIGuardrail(redactor=…) redacts PII in string fields via any Redactor InjectionGuardrail() a conservative prompt-injection lexicon DenyListGuardrail(patterns, …) caller-supplied deny list SizeGuardrail(max_chars, field=…) an input length cap PatternGuardrail(patterns, …) the generic regex form

block raises GuardrailViolation out of arun() (or drops that generation under isolate_errors=True); flag records reactifact_guardrail_triggered_total and lets the artifact through. Redaction runs in order, so a PIIGuardrail can scrub text before an InjectionGuardrail sees it. Guardrails apply to agent-produced artifacts; call policy.evaluate(data, context) yourself to screen a seeded input.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
A Principal (the user/tenant/service a run acts for) plus a policy gating what it may do:

from reactifact.authz import PermissionPolicy, Principal

resources = RuntimeResources(
    principal=Principal(id="alice", capabilities=("analyst",)),
    authorizer=PermissionPolicy(
        {"analyst": {"run:*", "create:Answer"}},
        default_allow=False,           # anonymous principals are denied
    ),
)

PermissionPolicy.grants maps a capability to "action:resource" patterns ("run:*", "create:*", "*"). The runtime enforces run (agent name) and create/update/delete (artifact type); the tool loop enforces execute (tool name); a step checks with the injected access: Access — access.can("read", id) to branch or access.require("read", id) to raise. Denial raises AuthorizationError.

docs.title: Quota
docs.text:
A Budget bounds a single turn; a quota bounds a principal across turns:

from reactifact.quota import Quota, QuotaTracker

resources = RuntimeResources(
    principal=Principal(id="acme"),
    quota=QuotaTracker(Quota(max_tokens=1_000_000, window_seconds=86_400)),
)

The runtime checks the quota at the start of each turn; an exhausted key sets RunOutcome.QUOTA_EXCEEDED and runs nothing. Usage is counted through the turn via QuotaLLM (cache hits are not charged). The default store is in-process — like LangChain's InMemoryRateLimiter, it does not coordinate across workers; pass store= (the tiny QuotaStore protocol) backed by shared state for a cluster.

docs.title: Relationship to the other primitives
docs.text: Redactor (trace redaction) and the destructive-tool approval gate predate this layer and still work on their own; trust & safety composes them into a policy surface and adds authorization and quota. MetricsTracer records guardrail triggers and quota-exceeded outcomes, so “why was this turn blocked” is answerable from the same traces and metrics as everything else.

docs.title: Scheduler semantics — the execution contract
docs.text:
This page is the execution contract of Runtime: how a run decides what executes, in what order, and when it stops. Every statement here describes behavior that already exists in the implementation (constitution §21–§24, §41–§44, §54, §58–§59, §69) — it is a specification, not a roadmap.

If the code and this page ever disagree, one of them is a bug. The tests in tests/test_scheduler_semantics.py pin the load-bearing claims so that a refactor that changes them fails CI instead of silently drifting this document.

docs.title: 1. Vocabulary
docs.text:
Term Meaning Turn One Runtime.arun() / arun_once() / astream() call. Bounded by a Budget and max_iterations.
